### DL-185: One Demo Studio for all of PMConcept7, and what the 5.6 Pro chat needs when it moves in

**Question:** Where do the concept's many demo controls live, and what has to change when the 5.6 Pro chat is ported into the new home?

**Why it came up:** PMConcept7 has tour and onboarding demo controls, home demos and, in the chat, many more, each with its own panel. Jared wants them in one place, and the Orchestrator and Planning Wizard redesigns will add many more. The new chat will be ported in after this redesign, and its colours, sizes, layers and hover tags have to fit PMConcept7's.

**What you get:**
- One Demo Studio for every PMConcept7 concept surface, modelled on the 5.6 Pro chat's: tour, onboarding, the chat's demos, the home demos, and later the Orchestrator and Planning Wizard pages. Each surface adds its controls to it instead of drawing its own demo panel.
- The Demo Studio is a concept tool: it never becomes a product control, setting, command or saved value.
- When the 5.6 Pro chat is ported: its Basic, Friendly and Glass colours are fixed to match PMConcept7's; its class names are namespaced; it sizes itself by its own column, not the window; it uses the page's one overlay layer and stacking order; PMConcept7's hover system owns its hover tags; its inline "Shell" box becomes a compact command card that opens the terminal tab; its pills and side stripes are removed; and its demo controls move into the Demo Studio.

**What it costs:**
- The chat port waits until this redesign is published, after the NieR showpiece, the 5.6 Pro chat round with its fonts, the Usage port, the left rail and the hover polish.
- Each surface's demo controls are moved once.

**Options considered:** A demo panel per surface (today's state, rejected by Jared). Porting the chat before the home redesign (rejected: the chat's tabs, width and tour step depend on the new home).

**What Jared asked (2026-10-09, in the T3 planning thread):**
- "we need to fix up the demo content and fold it into a centralized demo studio system for the rest of the pmconcept7 systems. Currently there are tour and onboarding controls, and some others, and a lot in chat. So that should all just be folded into one demo studio(like 5.6 chat's system). When I redesign the orchestrator page and planning wizard pages,(not now) those will need a lot of demo controls too so that can fold into that system."
- On the chat's colours: "we would need to fix its theme colors as you said".
- The rest is the planning thread's recommendation, which Jared accepted without change.

**What the spec now says:**
1. **One Demo Studio** (`Plans/FinalGUISpec.md#F3-649`, `Plans/DRY_Rules.md#DR-070`), lab only as `Plans/assistant-chat-design.md#ACD-474` already rules for the chat's.
2. **The chat port's requirements** (`Plans/assistant-chat-design.md#ACD-501`), and the chat's openings, width, History flyout, command card and Teacher explanations (`Plans/assistant-chat-design.md#ACD-500`).
3. **Order:** the concept work runs in its own package now; publishing into PMConcept7 comes after the NieR showpiece, the 5.6 Pro chat round with fonts, the Usage port, the left rail and the hover polish; the chat port follows this redesign.

### DL-186: Dashboards run on the Usage board engine, one board per tab, saved per project, with presets you can save

> Superseded in part by DL-287, DL-292 (2026-11-03). Existing Project boards remain per Project; a separate tagged application board uses the same engine and limits, and conversion never overwrites destination boards. Earlier ruling text and quoted user words are retained as history.

**Question:** Now that dashboard tabs run on the Usage page's widget board, what happens to the old Home widgets, where is each board kept, and what can a person do with a dashboard?

**Why it came up:** DL-180 made the dashboard an ordinary tab that can show every Usage widget and said it would run on the Usage board engine once that engine could run several boards at once. The panels thread built that second step on 2026-10-10 and brought Jared thirteen questions (P1 to P13) about the old Home widgets, ranges, presets, storage and the tour. Jared also answered an earlier question from the Plans thread: may a person make, rename or delete a dashboard (PLN-4)?

**What you get:**
- Every dashboard tab is its own board on the Usage board engine: Home, Metrics and Monitoring are built in, and you can make as many more as you like ("Dashboard 2" and on, or your own name). Agents stays a board the dashboard draws itself.
- A new dashboard starts empty. Home, Metrics and Monitoring start from their own sets of Usage widgets.
- Each dashboard has its own time range and scope (5 hours, 24 hours, 7 days or 30 days; all accounts, work, personal, or one provider), kept with that board.
- Reset puts a board back to its own default. Start from offers the board's default, each of the Usage page's 13 room sets, the dashboard starter, and any preset you saved. You can save a board's arrangement as your own preset, rename it or delete it; presets are yours across projects.
- You can rename or delete a dashboard you made (with a confirm). Home, Metrics, Monitoring and Agents can be reset but never deleted.
- Each board's widgets are kept per project. A dashboard you closed keeps its board while you can still reopen it, and forgets it once it leaves the reopen list. A saved named layout keeps the boards of the dashboards it holds (up to 64 KB; a bigger one is saved without its boards, and says so).
- Moving and resizing widgets behaves exactly as on the Usage page: other cards fall into empty space when you let go, and Tidy repacks a board in one step.
- Live updates and "Play the next hour" run on dashboards too, and a dashboard you cannot see does no work. A dashboard's first appearance plays the calm reading-order entrance. Details on a widget opens the Usage page with that widget's inspector.
- Boards sit on the Home tab's own surface, not the Usage page's background.
- The old Home widgets (run progress, lanes, results) leave Home until the Orchestrator page is redesigned. The Guided Tour's widget step now teaches adding Upcoming resets to the Home dashboard.

**What it costs:**
- Run progress, lanes and results are not on Home until Orchestrator widgets join the board engine.
- Every board is one more stored record per project; deleting a dashboard you made deletes its widgets.

**Options considered:** Keeping the old Home widgets as a "Home (current)" board until the Orchestrator redesign (Jared chose to drop them now, option B). Dashboards following the Usage page's range and scope (Jared chose their own). Boards shared across projects (Jared chose per project). Showing the Usage page's background behind a board (Jared chose Home's tab surface). A new dashboard starting from the dashboard starter set (Jared chose empty, with the starter as a Start from choice).

**What Jared asked (2026-10-10, relayed by the planning thread):**
- P1, the old Home widgets: option B, drop them now.
- P2: each dashboard has its own range and scope. P3: widget command payloads stay as they are, but boards, the catalogue and the layout record are designed for several sources (Usage now, the Orchestrator after its redesign, others later). P4: Reset offers the board's default and the 13 room sets through the existing reset command with a field naming the set, and you can save your own preset. P5: saved per project. P6: a closed board is forgotten when it leaves the reopen list, and named layouts keep board contents. P7: the reading-order entrance on first show. P8: Details goes to the Usage page's inspector. P9: Agents stays drawn by the dashboard. P10: the tour teaches Upcoming resets. P11: Home's tab surface. P12: live beats and Play the next hour on dashboards too. P13: the sets as built, and a new dashboard starts empty.
- PLN-4 (D35): "With savable presets." Custom dashboards can be made, renamed and deleted; Home, Metrics, Monitoring and Agents can be reset but not deleted.
- The storage key, the set names, the preset record and the rename and delete wiring are what the panels thread built, recorded as such. The 64 KB snapshot limit is the panels lead's proposal, adopted by the Plans lead.

**What the spec now says:**
1. **Dashboard boards** (`Plans/Widget_System.md#WS-030`, rewritten): per-project keys, the board ids, the Home host and sources, Reset and Start from with `set_id`, presets, rename, delete and reset, the reopen-list rule and named-layout snapshots; `#WS-019` (gravity and Tidy on every board) and `#WS-020` amended; `Plans/usage-feature.md` (live beats on dashboards).
2. **The dashboard tab** (`Plans/FinalGUISpec.md#F3-638`) and the Guided Tour's widget step (`Plans/Planning_Wizard.md#PWIZ-035`, `Plans/FinalGUISpec.md#F3-521`).
3. **Commands and wiring** (`Plans/UI_Command_Catalog.md#UCC-200`, `Plans/Wiring_Matrix.md#WM-090`): `cmd.widget.reset_layout` gains `set_id`; range and scope, and saving, renaming and deleting presets, are typed local actions; rename and delete reuse the tab commands.
4. **Storage** (`Plans/storage-plan.md`, `Plans/storage_value_registry.json`): the per-project board family and the per-user preset family.

### DL-187: Ten answers on the chat, the Debug Console, terminal tabs, saved scrollback, notifications and shells

> Superseded in part by DL-281, DL-287 (2026-11-03). Shell and persisted default choices consume their actual declared levels/Computer. Live session, scrollback/secret limits and pop-out non-persistence remain unchanged. Earlier ruling text and quoted user words are retained as history.

**Question:** The home redesign left ten questions for Jared, each with an interim rule in canon (PLN-1 to PLN-10). What are his answers?

**Why it came up:** Wave 1 of the home redesign canon (DL-180 to DL-185) landed with interim rules where Jared had not yet answered. He answered all ten on 2026-10-10.

**What you get:**
- A chat you popped out comes back in its column after a restart (D32).
- One Debug Console tab, with a sub-tab for each debug session (D33).
- Terminal tabs show no colour or icon choices on the tab strip for now; they will be redesigned with Puppet Master's neon glyph system (D34).
- Saved terminal scrollback has well-known secrets (API keys, bearer tokens and JWTs, key-named assignments, private-key blocks) replaced before it is written to disk; the live screen keeps the original (D36).
- Saved scrollback has a total cap of 512 MiB across every terminal; past it, the oldest saved scrollback goes first. Each terminal keeps its own 64 MiB (D37).
- A program's notification in a terminal raises a system notification while Puppet Master is in the background, at most one every 3 seconds per terminal, and each terminal can be muted from its More menu (D38).
- The "+" menu lists the shells installed on the computer, with SSH hosts in their own submenu (D39).
- Chat stays a left-rail entry; it shows or hides the chat column (D40).
- The Chat Layout setting retires: a stored Overlay or Detached value is ignored and cleared, with no pop-out and no notice.

**What it costs:**
- Scrubbing can replace something that only looked like a secret; the live screen still shows it.
- Terminal tab colours and icons wait for the glyph system.

**Options considered:** For each question the interim rule canon carried (a popped-out chat reopening popped out; one tab per debug session; no cap; no notifications) and the alternatives in the question set.

**What Jared asked (2026-10-10, answering the question set, relayed by the scheduler):** PLN-1 "a popped-out chat starts back in its column after a restart"; PLN-2 one Debug tab with a sub-tab per session; PLN-3 "redesign them" (terminal tab colours and icons, now part of the glyph system); PLN-4 see DL-186; PLN-5 scrub well-known secret formats from saved scrollback, the live screen keeps the original; PLN-6 a total cap across terminals (for example 512 MiB), oldest first, 64 MiB per terminal stays; PLN-7 system notifications while the app is in the background, with a per-terminal mute; PLN-8 installed shells, SSH hosts in a submenu; PLN-9 chat stays a rail entry that shows or hides the column; PLN-10 Addendum 2 renumbered to D29-D31. The 3-second limit, the scrub patterns and the fixed 512 MiB are the terminal thread's build, recorded by the Plans lead; retiring Chat Layout is the planning thread's ruling under D3 and D32.

**What the spec now says:**
1. **Chat** (`Plans/FinalGUISpec.md#F3-637`, `#F3-042`; `Plans/storage-plan.md#SP-330`): the pop-out is never saved; the rail's Chat entry shows or hides the column (`cmd.panel.switch`); `general.visual.chat-layout-mode` retires (`Plans/Settings_System.md#SSYS-050`).

**Question:** May the one event every panel and tab change records, `workspace.layout_changed`, move to the payload the universal panels need?

**Why it came up:** DL-180 makes every committed panel and tab change emit `workspace.layout_changed`. Its registered payload, 1.1.0, still describes the old Home of four editor panels, docks and terminal sections. Moving a registered event family moves the Event Authority checkpoint, which Jared approves himself (DL-039, DL-045), so wave 1 landed with the move recorded as pending.

**What you get:**
- `workspace.layout_changed` is registered at family revision 2.0.0 with the payload of `Plans/Contracts_V0.md#CV-361`: a `change` field naming what happened, the panels, tabs and splits it touched, both revisions and who did it.
- Registry checkpoint = approve `Plans/event_family_registry.json` revision `2026-10-09.1` (43 families; `workspace.layout_changed` payload 2.0.0) as the PNC-019 baseline, superseding the pinned `2026-09-25.1`.
- Events already written at 1.1.0 stay readable and are never rewritten.

**What it costs:**
- The checkpoint's evidence and the readiness receipt are refreshed by the next reseal.

**Options considered:** Keeping 1.1.0 and stretching it to the new model (it has no field for a tab, a split or a change kind).

**What Jared asked (2026-10-10, about 21:20 UTC, in the planning thread):** "approved".

**What the spec now says:**
1. **The registry and its checkpoint** (`Plans/event_family_registry.json`, `scripts/pm_pnc019_currentness.py`, the event fixtures).
2. **The payload** (`Plans/Contracts_V0.md#CV-361`, `Plans/event_payloads/workspace_layout_changed_v2.schema.json`), no longer pending.
3. **The PM7 fixtures** validate against the 2.0.0 payload.

**What each rule means for you**

| Rule | What it means | Limits that come with it |
|---|---|---|
| **Keep** | Never expires by age or by count. For a project's records, only "Delete Puppet Master project data" removes them ("Remove project from list" does not). It outlives the file, persona or chat it describes: deleting a chat purges the chat's content, not these records. | No count limit. If storage runs short, new records are refused rather than old ones dropped. Disk budgets still apply. |
| **7 years** | 2,555 days. | At most 2,000,000 per project. Past that, new records are **refused**; old ones are not dropped. Records that belong to no project need a counting bucket of their own (see **G05**). |
| **Run year** | One year after the run finishes. | 1,000,000 per run and 5,000,000 per project, then the history continues in a linked successor. Needs a real run. |
| **Chat** | Kept as long as its chat exists. | 250,000 per chat, then a linked continuation; nothing is dropped. Deleting the chat hides the history at once, purges it within 24 hours and from backups within 30 days. A hold delays the purge but never makes it visible again. The policy is written only on the unlanded Storage retention branch so far. |
| **Coordination** | 180 days after the run finishes. | 1,000,000 per project; past that, the oldest are dropped first. |
| **90 days** | 90 days. | 2,000,000 per project. Only expired records that no hold protects are removed; nothing is dropped early to make room. If the cap is reached before anything has expired, new records are **refused**, as with 7 years. No policy object exists yet; choosing it means Storage creates one with exactly these terms. |
| **Debug 30** | 30 days (only offered as an alternative below). | 10,000 per project; past that, the oldest are dropped first. |
| **Worktree year** | One year after the worktree is released (only **G24**). | 100,000 per project; past that, the oldest are dropped first. |

For every rule: legal holds, recovery anchors, the automatic keep on each project's latest 25 runs, live references and backups override expiry. In Settings, Advanced > Storage & Retention lets you lengthen history and diagnostic windows, never shorten them below these.

Two of the 88 are retired and need no rule (`coordination.debug_mirror_exported`, `dashboard.widget_added`).
  - The 51 Browser names are among the 88: Storage already splits them 28 Keep (metadata only) and 23 Run year (SP-262). The Storage owner wrote that split with the Browser work; you never ruled on Browser retention on a card. If you want to, say so in your reply.

**The 185 still open**

These are candidate names, counted before the naming choices on Card 2. A rule applies only to names that survive. If you approve Card 2 as recommended, 11 names leave this table (7 memory names in **G03**, two Browser names in **G10** and two Settings names in **G22**), leaving 174. The raw survey's original split (87 named, 68 answered, 186 open) is kept in the evidence; `scheduler.pass` moved from open to named after the review.

The recommendations follow one pattern:
- history that belongs to a chat goes with the chat (as you chose in DL-084 and DL-092);
- machine history of a run lasts a year after the run (as DL-086);
- your own actions and edits on lasting project objects are kept, holding names, IDs and references only, never file, document, persona or memory bodies. **What it costs.** "Chat" and "90 days" need two policy objects (the Chat one is written on the unlanded Storage retention branch; 90 days is new). Keep groups never expire by age or count; they hold names and references, so they stay small, but they count against disk budgets and refuse new records under storage pressure. 7-year groups refuse new records past 2,000,000 per project. **Exact approved option text from the presented cards:**

- **A (recommended):** Approve the complete proposal below. Keep the six probe labels and a separate cleanup result. Save each actual change in either value once, with its reason and before/after values. Re-reading, reprocessing old history, or repeating an unchanged result creates no duplicate change entry. A failure proved to have left nothing ends as **Cleaned / Not needed** and records that transition; it does not sit forever at Planned. Failed collection does not excuse earlier installed changes. You see every outstanding cleanup and outcome.

**Approved scope and conditions from the presented cards:**

**A’s proposed meanings:** A lane is one identified set of temporary changes on one target. Cleanup/rollback means undoing those changes and removing temporary connections. A durable fix is an explicitly accepted lasting code change, distinct from temporary debugging. Planned = installation not complete; Active = installed and ready; Collecting = gathering evidence; Cleanup pending = removal owed or underway; Cleanup failed = a removal attempt failed; Cleaned = this probe is finished with no temporary changes or debug connections left. Cleanup results are **Not needed** (nothing required undoing), **Pending** (undoing is still owed), **Succeeded** (undoing was verified), **Failed** (the attempt failed), and **Superseded** (responsibility handed over, with remaining work still visible). Pending while Active/Collecting means later removal is owed, not that removal is running.

**A’s complete allowed changes** (each arrow saves a change entry; “/” separates probe status and cleanup result):

| What happens | Before → after | What is recorded or preserved |
|---|---|---|
| Installation succeeds | Planned / Not needed → Active / Pending | Installation succeeded; later removal is owed. |
| Evidence collection starts | Active / Pending → Collecting / Pending | Collection began. |
| Collection pauses or finishes while the probe remains installed | Collecting / Pending → Active / Pending | Collection outcome; removal is still owed. |
| Installation or collection fails, or work ends, and proof shows the entire lane never needed any undoing and has no leftover change, process or attachment | Planned / Not needed, Active / Pending, or Collecting / Pending → Cleaned / Not needed | Save failure/end reason and no-leftovers proof. “Collection changed nothing” alone is insufficient if an earlier installation remains. |
| Installation partly fails, collection fails, or work resolves/is cancelled with known or possible leftovers | Planned / Not needed, Active / Pending, or Collecting / Pending → Cleanup pending / Pending | Save reason, exact remaining obligations and recovery link; attempt cleanup automatically. |
| Inspection after an uncertain failure proves that removal was never needed | Cleanup pending / Pending, Cleanup pending / Superseded, or Cleanup failed / Failed → Cleaned / Not needed | Save whole-lane proof that no temporary change, process or attachment ever required undoing. Retain the earlier uncertainty/failure; never relabel actual removal as Not needed. |
| Removal or undoing temporary changes succeeds and no temporary resources remain | Cleanup pending / Pending → Cleaned / Succeeded | Save proof of removal, including detaching temporary debugger/profiler connections. |
| Removal, rollback or detach fails | Cleanup pending / Pending → Cleanup failed / Failed | Save remaining files, settings, processes or connections; show failure even when disk files are clean. |
| An authorized cleanup retry begins | Cleanup failed / Failed → Cleanup pending / Pending | Save retry and attempt number; at most two retries after the initial attempt. |
| Retry succeeds or fails | Cleanup pending / Pending → Cleaned / Succeeded or Cleanup failed / Failed | Same success proof or visible leftovers as above. |
| Newer work replaces an unfinished probe, or responsibility passes to an explicitly approved durable fix, while cleanup may still be owed | Planned / Not needed, Active / Pending, Collecting / Pending, Cleanup pending / Pending, or Cleanup failed / Failed → Cleanup pending / Superseded | Save old/new responsible owners, linked work, remaining obligations and retry count. Handoff proves no removal. Replacement triggers automatic cleanup; promotion uses the existing approval route. |
| Receiving owner starts or resumes that cleanup | Cleanup pending / Superseded → Cleanup pending / Pending | Save acceptance and resumed removal; handoff never resets the retry ceiling. Resuming after a failed attempt is a retry under that ceiling. |
| Receiving owner accepts cleanup after an earlier failed attempt but no retry is authorized or both retries are already used | Cleanup pending / Superseded → Cleanup failed / Failed | Save acceptance and the still-failed outcome; do not run another attempt or claim cleanup succeeded. |
| Newer work replaces a lane proved never to have needed cleanup | Planned / Not needed, Active / Pending, or Collecting / Pending → Cleaned / Not needed | Save replacement reason and linked work with proof there are no leftovers anywhere in that lane. |

The initial probe record is **Planned / Not needed**; creation is not a previous-to-next change. No other status/result pair or transition is allowed by A. Failed cleanup with no authorized retry, or both retries used, stays **Cleanup failed / Failed** with leftovers visible. A requirement to preserve a change or an accepted follow-up does not claim Cleaned; handed-over cleanup stays **Cleanup pending / Superseded** until its receiving owner acts. A second handoff waits for that acceptance; reprocessing the same handoff adds nothing. Failed or uncertain handoff leaves previous responsibility and status in place. A Cleaned probe never restarts; later installation gets a new linked probe. No new code-changing debugging starts on the same target until leftovers are resolved, undone or explicitly promoted into the durable fix. Two investigations may not add overlapping temporary changes. Recovery snapshots taken before temporary changes, exact setting restoration and hiding secrets remain required. This chooses no additional history lifetime.

**Sources:** `MAIN:Plans/feature-list.md:31-37`; `MAIN:Plans/MiscPlan.md:1323-1343`; `MAIN:Plans/assistant-chat-design.md:1189-1207`; `MAIN:Plans/MiscPlan.md:6427-6427`; `evidence:reviews/DDBG-sol/REVIEW-cycle3.md:57-77`; `evidence:reviews/DDBG-sol/REVIEW-astra-3.md:121-122`.

**Supersession and boundaries:** Approves the complete 3.c proposal, including every status/result meaning, transition, whole-lane no-leftovers proof, cleanup handoff and retry ceiling reproduced here. Supersedes the incomplete pairing and transition rules only as specified. A Cleaned probe never restarts, unresolved cleanup remains visible, and this choice selects no additional history lifetime.

**Card item:** E-CARDS-2 **4.f**. **Question:** When may Doctor save its one-time notice that the optional custom browser tool is not configured?

Jared’s verbatim answer:

> i approve all of it

SourceRef: T3 thread 1338d738-7bb4-47b2-852e-38a876cb8521 (pm7-build), 2026-11-05T04:33:13Z, relayed to stream E by pm7-build (mail 1105043336-06d3). Cards as presented: `/mnt/Cursor/PuppetMaster-Evidence/event-authority-20261104/decision-answers/E-CARDS-2.as-presented-6db25be3.md`, SHA-256 `6db25be3dd290ab0083af482383e469a78dc109a037ad0fd0ece5d8f15679b30`. Source aliases below are pinned by the presented deck’s Source revisions section.

Coordinator pm7-build’s relayed reading (not Jared’s words): item **4.f** selects **A**. The presented deck’s fast-reply rule is: "`approve all` selects **A** on all 38 items."

**Exact approved option text from the presented cards:**

- **A (recommended):** Save the notice the first time Doctor’s readiness check finds the setting for that optional custom browser tool absent for that Project. An earlier run with the setting present leaves the chance unused. Once issued, the notice never resets for configuration edits or removing/re-adding the setting. If an older backup cannot prove that, do not guess and show a duplicate. Later checks still save their ordinary check result.

> i approve all of it

Answer file: `/mnt/Cursor/PuppetMaster-Evidence/event-authority-20261104/decision-answers/ANSWERS_E-CARDS-2_20261105.md`. Cards as presented: `/mnt/Cursor/PuppetMaster-Evidence/event-authority-20261104/decision-answers/E-CARDS-2.as-presented-6db25be3.md`, SHA-256 `6db25be3dd290ab0083af482383e469a78dc109a037ad0fd0ece5d8f15679b30`. Source aliases below are pinned by the presented deck’s Source revisions section.

Coordinator pm7-build’s relayed reading (not Jared’s words): item **6.a** selects **A**. The presented deck’s fast-reply rule is: "`approve all` selects **A** on all 38 items."

**Exact approved option text from the presented cards:**

- **A (recommended):** Keep the oldest eligible memory by original creation time, breaking a tie by the unchanging note ID. Preserve every original evidence reference and the record of which copies were merged. If pin protection prevents that merge, skip it. You keep the earliest note ID and its history links.

**Approved scope and conditions from the presented cards:**

Deletion stays your action. Pins, versions, audit history and evidence references stay protected. A protected memory does not become mergeable through these choices. **6.a/6.b** govern duplicates; **6.c/6.d** govern separate archive jobs. The **usefulness score is a computed ranking, not a percentage of usefulness**. Its existing formula combines how strongly a memory matches keyword and meaning searches, how often/recently it was used, and its kind/status. Its contribution falls with age at the existing rate for that kind; Done memories lose weight faster. Each missing search score contributes zero. A pin protects the memory before scoring. Both age AND score must qualify, using values captured when the job chooses memories. A crowded list alone never triggers archiving. Automatic jobs and panel buttons stay unavailable until your answer is applied and all remaining definition, review and recording approvals pass.

**Sources:** `MAIN:Plans/assistant-memory-subsystem.md:398-412`; `DMEM:Plans/assistant-memory-subsystem.md:3156-3174`; `ANS:Plans/Decision_Log.md:4514-4516`; `evidence:reviews/DMEM-sol/REVIEW-astra-2.md:74-80`; `evidence:reviews/DMEM-sol/REVIEW-cycle4.md:3-7`.

**Supersession and boundaries:** Resolves the duplicate sweep survivor choice left open by DL-402: oldest eligible original creation time, then unchanging note ID. Pin protection can require skipping the merge. Evidence references and merge lineage remain; DL-402’s separate monthly-summary and prune/archive rules stand.

### DL-453: 47 lasting-change histories stay permanently

**Card item:** E-CARDS-3 **1.a**. **Question:** Should these 47 histories stay permanently, for seven years or for 90 days?

Jared’s verbatim answer:

> The rest I will defer to your recommendations.

SourceRef: T3 thread 1338d738-7bb4-47b2-852e-38a876cb8521 (program thread pm7-build), 2026-11-05T17:02:41Z, relayed to the stream E lead by pm7-build (mail 1105170345-d5f2). Answer file: `/mnt/Cursor/PuppetMaster-Evidence/event-authority-20261104/decision-answers/ANSWERS_E-CARDS-3_20261105.md`. Cards as presented: `/mnt/Cursor/PuppetMaster-Evidence/event-authority-20261104/decision-answers/E-CARDS-3.as-presented-a7d00c73.md`, SHA-256 `a7d00c733539daa94b8a85bd9725d3658a4bbfcd7c1927507db0a4ace626db1f`. Source aliases below are the presented deck’s own S-aliases, resolved inline in each Sources line.

Coordinator pm7-build’s relayed reading (not Jared’s words): “So A on all 12 items of E-CARDS-3.md.” Item **1.a** selects **A**. The presented deck’s fast-reply rule is: "`approve all` selects **A** on all twelve items."

**Approved scope and conditions from the presented cards:**

- **Permanent:** no expiry by age or count. The already defined safe metadata, identifiers, hashes and references stay in these entries; their payload fields and redaction rules do not change. Deleting the described file, object or chat does not remove this separate history or preserve the deleted content. For Project records, explicit **Delete Puppet Master project data** removes them under existing protection rules; **Remove project from list** does not. Application records remain subject to their existing authorized data-deletion rules; this deck adds no app-data delete control. Finite disk budgets still apply: storage pressure refuses new history writes.

For every option, protection for the latest 25 runs applies where the existing rule requires it. Holds and required references can keep history past its ordinary expiry; they grant no visibility or access. Existing Settings may lengthen an eligible history window, never shorten it below the chosen minimum. Original approvals, saved results, prompt text, documents, media and backup generations keep their own lifetimes.

**Exact approved option text from the presented cards:**

- **A (recommended):** Keep all 47 types **permanently**, using the deletion and storage-pressure rules above. ### DL-459: Browser reader checkpoints keep a replaced copy seven days

**Card item:** E-CARDS-3 **6.b**. **Question:** How long should the two Browser history readers keep a replaced reader copy: seven days, 90 days or seven years?

Jared’s verbatim answer:

> The rest I will defer to your recommendations.

SourceRef: T3 thread 1338d738-7bb4-47b2-852e-38a876cb8521 (program thread pm7-build), 2026-11-05T17:02:41Z, relayed to the stream E lead by pm7-build (mail 1105170345-d5f2). Answer file: `/mnt/Cursor/PuppetMaster-Evidence/event-authority-20261104/decision-answers/ANSWERS_E-CARDS-3_20261105.md`. Cards as presented: `/mnt/Cursor/PuppetMaster-Evidence/event-authority-20261104/decision-answers/E-CARDS-3.as-presented-a7d00c73.md`, SHA-256 `a7d00c733539daa94b8a85bd9725d3658a4bbfcd7c1927507db0a4ace626db1f`. Source aliases below are the presented deck’s own S-aliases, resolved inline in each Sources line.

Coordinator pm7-build’s relayed reading (not Jared’s words): “So A on all 12 items of E-CARDS-3.md.” Item **6.b** selects **A**. The presented deck’s fast-reply rule is: "`approve all` selects **A** on all twelve items."

**Approved scope and conditions from the presented cards:**

**Common boundary for all options:** keep the **current copy while that exact reader needs it**, with no age expiry while current. Keep at most **three copies together per reader, for one Project or for one Server's history outside Projects**: the current copy plus any copies being built or replaced. The two readers have separate three-copy limits; no limit resets per source chat, and there is no 2,000,000-entry event allowance here. When a genuine replacement makes a new copy current, or the reader is withdrawn, the previously current copy's clock starts at that moment; saving progress, retries and restores never start or restart it. Remove a replaced copy only when its chosen window has ended and it has no hold or required reference. A copy that was being built and was discarded without ever becoming current is removed through the existing authorized cleanup once it is shown never to have been used and its references and protections are cleared; it needs no window and no made-up retirement time. If all three copies must remain, refuse another build or replacement until a copy can lawfully be removed. An existing current copy may keep saving progress only while it still passes the reader's checks against the retained original history. If the reader needs a rebuild to pass those checks, keep the last saved copy and show the affected reader as unavailable until a lawful rebuild is possible. A lost copy means checking retained original history again; it never recreates missing original events.

Chat deletion still hides the deleted chat's history immediately. Purge its unheld references from active reader copies within **24 hours** and backups within **30 days**; if a mixed copy cannot satisfy that by removing those references lawfully, discard the whole affected copy and rebuild only from retained, permitted original history. A missing complete source makes that reader unavailable, not permission to resurrect deleted history. Holds can delay physical purge without restoring access. Deleting the owning Project/app data follows its existing rules. These source-deletion limits override a copy's remaining ordinary window; none of A/B/C lengthens an event, receipt, page or chat lifetime.

**Exact approved option text from the presented cards:**

- **A (recommended):** Keep a replaced copy for **seven days (604,800 seconds)** after it stops being current, under the common rules above. This follows the existing rule for disposable reader checkpoints. You keep a short recovery history; older unprotected copies are rebuilt when needed.

**Sources:** `S1353` (8791f549ae15:Plans/Section15_MVP_Promoted_Features_Spec.md:13913-13920); `S1354` (8791f549ae15:Plans/Section15_MVP_Promoted_Features_Spec.md:13965-13972); `S1355` (57c28f706e10:Plans/storage-plan.md:19584-19605); `S1359` (57c28f706e10:Plans/storage_value_registry.json:175-190); `S1360` (57c28f706e10:Plans/storage-plan.md:20297-20330); `S1361` (57c28f706e10:Plans/storage-plan.md:21215-21221); `S1366` (9b76338594c6:Plans/storage-plan.md:17423-17425); `S1352` (drafts/DS15/DS15.md:92-103).

**Supersession and boundaries:** Assigns the two Browser reader checkpoint keys a seven-day window for a replaced copy under the common three-copy boundary, with the current copy kept while its reader needs it. This is a saved-value rule, not an event allowance, and it extends no source event, receipt, page or chat lifetime.

**Proposed common boundary for A on each item:** count and store the named history in **one Puppet Master Server's saved application history, shared by all its connected Clients**. No count resets per chat, Client, person, root, restart or workflow; a record belonging to a Project stays solely under its already approved Project rule. Shared counting grants no access to another person's history or linked content. The three bounded A choices each propose their **own separate 2,000,000-entry allowance** for that one type, separate from each other, the other items and every previously approved application allowance. The two permanent A choices have **no age or count limit**, as already chosen; imposing a 2,000,000-entry expiry on proof would reopen that answer. Every choice still obeys the Server's existing finite disk budget, with no new byte limit or reserved disk allocation.

**Proposed deletion and protection rule within each A:** ordinary file, chat or Project deletion, removing a Project from the list, disconnecting a Client, and history reaching capacity do not authorize deletion of this separate application history. Automatic expiry cleanup may remove only expired entries free of **every** legal/investigation hold, active source/reference, recovery, preserved/recent-run, rollback, maintenance and protected-backup obligation. Permanent proof has no automatic expiry cleanup.

Earlier removal requires an **explicit, separately confirmed deletion request from a person authorized for that Server's data**, naming that Server and this item's exact FileSafe application history. Existing Storage ownership, permission, scope and destructive-intent checks must authorize it; a chat owner, a reference or a Project-delete request alone is insufficient. Persist the content-free deletion record and hide the selected history immediately; purge unprotected active copies within **24 hours** and backup bytes within **30 days**. The protections above preserve required custody until lawfully released, without restoring visibility or clearing a hold. Restore applies the deletion record before exposing history. If identity, permission, scope or protected references cannot be proved, refuse the deletion. This is a proposed authorization rule for the selected history, using the existing scoped Storage deletion mechanism; it grants no application-wide wipe permission or new delete control. Owners must bind that exact rule before recording. Original approvals, action results, snapshots, recovery journals and linked bodies keep their independent retention and access rules.

**Exact approved option text from the presented cards:**

- **A (recommended):** Give this one type of **blocked-command history its own 2,000,000-entry allowance outside Projects**, across the one Server and all connected Clients above. Keep the already chosen **2,555 days** from the saved original refusal or startup-failure result's first successful save that survives a restart. Retry, reprocessing, restart recovery, restore and later observations never reset that original clock. Use this item's proposed deletion/protection rule above. Only expired unprotected entries free ordinary capacity; never evict unexpired or protected entries to make room. If the count is full with no eligible expiry, or the existing disk budget prevents a safe save, refuse the new history entry. You get seven-year application troubleshooting history; expired unprotected entries can disappear, while ordinary file/chat/Project deletion does not shorten this separate history's window. A separately authorized confirmed deletion follows the rule above.

**Sources:** `S1276` (c81490e38cdd:Plans/Decision_Log.md:4880-4905); `S1377` (a10cfa6d834f:Plans/storage-plan.md:29528-29530); `S1370` (decision-answers/E-CARDS-2.as-presented-6db25be3.md:107-174); `S1388` (c81490e38cdd:Plans/Decision_Log.md:4784-4806); `S1382` (9b76338594c6:Plans/storage-plan.md:17491-17504); `S1375` (reviews/DF-sol/REVIEW-cycle7.md:71-99); `S1386` (57c28f706e10:Plans/storage-plan.md:17504-17516).

**Supersession and boundaries:** Completes the outside-Project counting, capacity and authorized-deletion rule that DL-422 expressly reserved for filesafe.command_denied: its own 2,000,000-entry Server-wide allowance under the already chosen 2,555-day clock and the scoped deletion/protection rule. The seven-year lifetime and Project rule are unchanged.

```yaml
canonical_text: '**Card item:** E-CARDS-2 **1.a**. **Question:** When does the 90-day history clock start?

  > i approve all of it

  reprocessing old history and recovering after a restart never restart the clock. You get a full 90 days of
  saved history even if recording was delayed.
```

### DL-422 - filesafe.command_denied is seven-year troubleshooting history

```yaml
plan_unit_id: DL-422
unit_type: decision
status: accepted
owner_doc: Plans/Decision_Log.md
canonical_text: '**Card item:** E-CARDS-2 **2.a**. **Question:** Is a blocked-command event lasting proof of
  a refusal or seven-year troubleshooting history?


  Jared’s verbatim answer:


  > i approve all of it


  SourceRef: T3 thread 1338d738-7bb4-47b2-852e-38a876cb8521 (pm7-build), 2026-11-05T04:33:13Z, relayed to stream
  E by pm7-build (mail 1105043336-06d3). Answer file: `/mnt/Cursor/PuppetMaster-Evidence/event-authority-20261104/decision-answers/ANSWERS_E-CARDS-2_20261105.md`.
  Cards as presented: `/mnt/Cursor/PuppetMaster-Evidence/event-authority-20261104/decision-answers/E-CARDS-2.as-presented-6db25be3.md`,
  SHA-256 `6db25be3dd290ab0083af482383e469a78dc109a037ad0fd0ece5d8f15679b30`. Source aliases below are pinned
  by the presented deck’s Source revisions section.


  Coordinator pm7-build’s relayed reading (not Jared’s words): item **2.a** selects **A**. The presented deck’s
  fast-reply rule is: "`approve all` selects **A** on all 38 items."


  **Exact approved option text from the presented cards:**


  - **A (recommended):** Keep this event about a command FileSafe refused as troubleshooting history for seven
  years under the limits above. It may disappear after expiry and protection checks; the original approval
  or action result keeps its own lifetime.


  **Approved scope and conditions from the presented cards:**


  For a seven-year choice, keep 2,555 days from the saved original refusal, override request or startup-failure
  result, up to 2,000,000 records per Project. Retrying a save, reprocessing old history or recovering after
  a restart never resets that clock. Remove only expired entries no investigation, active reference, recovery
  or backup protects; refuse new entries when full and none may expire. Supporting approvals, source snapshots
  and recovery logs keep their own lifetimes.


  **“Permanent” means:** no expiry by age or count. Deleting the file or chat an entry describes does not remove
  that entry. For Project entries, explicit **Delete Puppet Master project data** removes them under existing
  deletion and protection rules; **Remove project from list** does not delete that data. If space runs out,
  refuse new entries instead of dropping old ones. These five choices add no counting or deletion rule for
  future entries outside Projects; each such version still needs its own exact approved rules before recording.


  **Sources:** `MAIN:Plans/storage-plan.md:17403-17410`; `DF:Plans/storage-plan.md:29530-29530`; `evidence:decision-answers/E-CARDS-1.as-presented-578a6774.md:42-42`;
```

### DL-429 - Debug probes preserve the complete status and cleanup transition proposal

```yaml
plan_unit_id: DL-429
unit_type: decision
status: accepted
owner_doc: Plans/Decision_Log.md
canonical_text: '**Card item:** E-CARDS-2 **3.c**. **Question:** Which temporary Debug-probe and cleanup changes
  should be saved?


  Jared’s verbatim answer:


  > i approve all of it


  SourceRef: T3 thread 1338d738-7bb4-47b2-852e-38a876cb8521 (pm7-build), 2026-11-05T04:33:13Z, relayed to stream
  E by pm7-build (mail 1105043336-06d3). Answer file: `/mnt/Cursor/PuppetMaster-Evidence/event-authority-20261104/decision-answers/ANSWERS_E-CARDS-2_20261105.md`.
  Cards as presented: `/mnt/Cursor/PuppetMaster-Evidence/event-authority-20261104/decision-answers/E-CARDS-2.as-presented-6db25be3.md`,
  SHA-256 `6db25be3dd290ab0083af482383e469a78dc109a037ad0fd0ece5d8f15679b30`. Source aliases below are pinned
  by the presented deck’s Source revisions section.


  Coordinator pm7-build’s relayed reading (not Jared’s words): item **3.c** selects **A**. The presented deck’s
  fast-reply rule is: "`approve all` selects **A** on all 38 items."


  **Exact approved option text from the presented cards:**


  - **A (recommended):** Approve the complete proposal below. Keep the six probe labels and a separate cleanup
  result. Save each actual change in either value once, with its reason and before/after values. Re-reading,
  reprocessing old history, or repeating an unchanged result creates no duplicate change entry. A failure proved
  to have left nothing ends as **Cleaned / Not needed** and records that transition; it does not sit forever
  at Planned. Failed collection does not excuse earlier installed changes. You see every outstanding cleanup
  and outcome.


  **Approved scope and conditions from the presented cards:**


  **A’s proposed meanings:** A lane is one identified set of temporary changes on one target. Cleanup/rollback
  means undoing those changes and removing temporary connections. A durable fix is an explicitly accepted lasting
  code change, distinct from temporary debugging. Planned = installation not complete; Active = installed and
  ready; Collecting = gathering evidence; Cleanup pending = removal owed or underway; Cleanup failed = a removal
  attempt failed; Cleaned = this probe is finished with no temporary changes or debug connections left. Cleanup
  results are **Not needed** (nothing required undoing), **Pending** (undoing is still owed), **Succeeded**
  (undoing was verified), **Failed** (the attempt failed), and **Superseded** (responsibility handed over,
  with remaining work still visible). Pending while Active/Collecting means later removal is owed, not that
  removal is running.


  **A’s complete allowed changes** (each arrow saves a change entry; “/” separates probe status and cleanup
  result):


  | What happens | Before → after | What is recorded or preserved |

  |---|---|---|

  | Installation succeeds | Planned / Not needed → Active / Pending | Installation succeeded; later removal
  is owed. |

  | Evidence collection starts | Active / Pending → Collecting / Pending | Collection began. |

  | Collection pauses or finishes while the probe remains installed | Collecting / Pending → Active / Pending
  | Collection outcome; removal is still owed. |

  | Installation or collection fails, or work ends, and proof shows the entire lane never needed any undoing
  and has no leftover change, process or attachment | Planned / Not needed, Active / Pending, or Collecting
  / Pending → Cleaned / Not needed | Save failure/end reason and no-leftovers proof. “Collection changed nothing”
  alone is insufficient if an earlier installation remains. |

  | Installation partly fails, collection fails, or work resolves/is cancelled with known or possible leftovers
  | Planned / Not needed, Active / Pending, or Collecting / Pending → Cleanup pending / Pending | Save reason,
  exact remaining obligations and recovery link; attempt cleanup automatically. |

  | Inspection after an uncertain failure proves that removal was never needed | Cleanup pending / Pending,
  Cleanup pending / Superseded, or Cleanup failed / Failed → Cleaned / Not needed | Save whole-lane proof that
  no temporary change, process or attachment ever required undoing. Retain the earlier uncertainty/failure;
  never relabel actual removal as Not needed. |

  | Removal or undoing temporary changes succeeds and no temporary resources remain | Cleanup pending / Pending
  → Cleaned / Succeeded | Save proof of removal, including detaching temporary debugger/profiler connections.
  |

  | Removal, rollback or detach fails | Cleanup pending / Pending → Cleanup failed / Failed | Save remaining
  files, settings, processes or connections; show failure even when disk files are clean. |

  | An authorized cleanup retry begins | Cleanup failed / Failed → Cleanup pending / Pending | Save retry and
  attempt number; at most two retries after the initial attempt. |

  | Retry succeeds or fails | Cleanup pending / Pending → Cleaned / Succeeded or Cleanup failed / Failed |
  Same success proof or visible leftovers as above. |

  | Newer work replaces an unfinished probe, or responsibility passes to an explicitly approved durable fix,
  while cleanup may still be owed | Planned / Not needed, Active / Pending, Collecting / Pending, Cleanup pending
  / Pending, or Cleanup failed / Failed → Cleanup pending / Superseded | Save old/new responsible owners, linked
  work, remaining obligations and retry count. Handoff proves no removal. Replacement triggers automatic cleanup;
  promotion uses the existing approval route. |

  | Receiving owner starts or resumes that cleanup | Cleanup pending / Superseded → Cleanup pending / Pending
  | Save acceptance and resumed removal; handoff never resets the retry ceiling. Resuming after a failed attempt
  is a retry under that ceiling. |

  | Receiving owner accepts cleanup after an earlier failed attempt but no retry is authorized or both retries
  are already used | Cleanup pending / Superseded → Cleanup failed / Failed | Save acceptance and the still-failed
  outcome; do not run another attempt or claim cleanup succeeded. |

  | Newer work replaces a lane proved never to have needed cleanup | Planned / Not needed, Active / Pending,
  or Collecting / Pending → Cleaned / Not needed | Save replacement reason and linked work with proof there
  are no leftovers anywhere in that lane. |


  The initial probe record is **Planned / Not needed**; creation is not a previous-to-next change. No other
  status/result pair or transition is allowed by A. Failed cleanup with no authorized retry, or both retries
  used, stays **Cleanup failed / Failed** with leftovers visible. A requirement to preserve a change or an
  accepted follow-up does not claim Cleaned; handed-over cleanup stays **Cleanup pending / Superseded** until
  its receiving owner acts. A second handoff waits for that acceptance; reprocessing the same handoff adds
  nothing. Failed or uncertain handoff leaves previous responsibility and status in place. A Cleaned probe
  never restarts; later installation gets a new linked probe. No new code-changing debugging starts on the
  same target until leftovers are resolved, undone or explicitly promoted into the durable fix. Two investigations
  may not add overlapping temporary changes. Recovery snapshots taken before temporary changes, exact setting
  restoration and hiding secrets remain required. This chooses no additional history lifetime.


  **Sources:** `MAIN:Plans/feature-list.md:31-37`; `MAIN:Plans/MiscPlan.md:1323-1343`; `MAIN:Plans/assistant-chat-design.md:1189-1207`;
  `MAIN:Plans/MiscPlan.md:6427-6427`; `evidence:reviews/DDBG-sol/REVIEW-cycle3.md:57-77`; `evidence:reviews/DDBG-sol/REVIEW-astra-3.md:121-122`.


  **Supersession and boundaries:** Approves the complete 3.c proposal, including every status/result meaning,
  transition, whole-lane no-leftovers proof, cleanup handoff and retry ceiling reproduced here. Supersedes
  the incomplete pairing and transition rules only as specified. A Cleaned probe never restarts, unresolved
  cleanup remains visible, and this choice selects no additional history lifetime.'
```

### DL-434 - Catalog updates wait for the next safe reload or start

```yaml
plan_unit_id: DL-434
unit_type: decision
status: accepted
owner_doc: Plans/Decision_Log.md
canonical_text: '**Card item:** E-CARDS-2 **4.d**. **Question:** When should a catalog update take effect in
  the listed uses?


  Jared’s verbatim answer:


  > i approve all of it


  SourceRef: T3 thread 1338d738-7bb4-47b2-852e-38a876cb8521 (pm7-build), 2026-11-05T04:33:13Z, relayed to stream
  E by pm7-build (mail 1105043336-06d3). Answer file: `/mnt/Cursor/PuppetMaster-Evidence/event-authority-20261104/decision-answers/ANSWERS_E-CARDS-2_20261105.md`.

  SHA-256 `6db25be3dd290ab0083af482383e469a78dc109a037ad0fd0ece5d8f15679b30`. Source aliases below are pinned
  by the presented deck’s Source revisions section.


  Coordinator pm7-build’s relayed reading (not Jared’s words): item **4.d** selects **A**. The presented deck’s
  fast-reply rule is: "`approve all` selects **A** on all 38 items."


  **Exact approved option text from the presented cards:**


  - **A (recommended):** For the listed uses, keep the current verified version and queue the update until
  the next safe reload or start allowed by the component that uses it. Save completion only when the new version
  takes effect. You keep using the old version until it is safe to switch.


  **Approved scope and conditions from the presented cards:**


  **Exact scope — derived by the writer from the current plans, corrected after the blind review.** These are
  practical uses or saved references whose update/removal timing is missing, not new stored states. “Persona”
  means a saved agent profile; a “hook” runs plugin code at a named app action. Installable MCP settings tell
  the app how to connect to an external tool server. Existing stricter outcomes are excluded.


  | Catalog item | Current use or reference | Unresolved choice |

  |---|---|---|

  | **Catalog-installed command** | Open in an edit session | When an update takes effect. |

  | **Catalog-installed command** | Named by another app component that requires replacement or confirmation
  but gives no update/removal timing | When an update takes effect. |

  | **Catalog-installed skill** | Selected for the current request before instructions are loaded or it is
  called; includes a request explicitly naming the skill with no saved agent profile | When an update takes
  effect. |

  | **Catalog-installed skill** | Instructions loaded for the current agent, or a validated skill call in progress
  | When an update takes effect. |

  | **Catalog-installed skill** | Named in a saved agent profile (Persona) | When an update takes effect. |

  | **Catalog-installed plugin or hook** | Enabled, not currently loaded | When an update takes effect. |

  | **Catalog-installed plugin or hook** | Loaded for the session, including plugin code currently running
  in response to an app action | When an update takes effect. |

  | **Catalog-installed plugin or hook** | Named in saved agent-profile settings | When an update takes effect.
  |

  | **Catalog-installed tool-server connection settings (MCP)** | Used by an enabled or configured tool server,
  or a working connection to it | When an update takes effect. |

  | **Catalog-installed tool-server connection settings (MCP)** | Named in saved agent-profile settings | When
  an update takes effect. |


  **Already settled outside this choice:** deleting a command open in an editor is refused; valid edits to
  the active theme apply immediately. Each in-progress request keeps the exact skill content/version it already
  selected, including before loading or invocation. Updates/removals cannot rewrite that saved request. Plugin
  versions still require any existing renewed approval and recovery after failed updates. Server connections
  still require valid credentials and the current connection version. Personal customizations and external-service
  data stay protected. No extra catalog item type is covered.
```

### DL-436 - Doctor’s skipped notice uses the first check that finds the setting absent

```yaml
plan_unit_id: DL-436
unit_type: decision
status: accepted
owner_doc: Plans/Decision_Log.md
canonical_text: '**Card item:** E-CARDS-2 **4.f**. **Question:** When may Doctor save its one-time notice that
  the optional custom browser tool is not configured?


  Jared’s verbatim answer:


  > i approve all of it


  SourceRef: T3 thread 1338d738-7bb4-47b2-852e-38a876cb8521 (pm7-build), 2026-11-05T04:33:13Z, relayed to stream
  E by pm7-build (mail 1105043336-06d3). Answer file: `/mnt/Cursor/PuppetMaster-Evidence/event-authority-20261104/decision-answers/ANSWERS_E-CARDS-2_20261105.md`.
  Cards as presented: `/mnt/Cursor/PuppetMaster-Evidence/event-authority-20261104/decision-answers/E-CARDS-2.as-presented-6db25be3.md`,
  SHA-256 `6db25be3dd290ab0083af482383e469a78dc109a037ad0fd0ece5d8f15679b30`. Source aliases below are pinned
  by the presented deck’s Source revisions section.


  Coordinator pm7-build’s relayed reading (not Jared’s words): item **4.f** selects **A**. The presented deck’s
  fast-reply rule is: "`approve all` selects **A** on all 38 items."


  **Exact approved option text from the presented cards:**


  - **A (recommended):** Save the notice the first time Doctor’s readiness check finds the setting for that
  optional custom browser tool absent for that Project. An earlier run with the setting present leaves the
  chance unused. Once issued, the notice never resets for configuration edits or removing/re-adding the setting.
  A clone or import gets a fresh chance only if it creates a separate new Project with its own saved ID. Restoring
  the same Project preserves whether the notice was already shown. If an older backup cannot prove that, do
  not guess and show a duplicate. Later checks still save their ordinary check result.


  **Sources:** `MAIN:Plans/newtools.md:498-511`; `DT:reports/event-authority-20261104/DT.md:272-273`; `evidence:reviews/DT-sol/REVIEW.md:118-122`;

  `evidence:reviews/DT-sol/REVIEW-cycle4.md:93-107`; `evidence:reviews/DT-sol/REVIEW-cycle5.md:7-7`.


  **Supersession and boundaries:** Resolves the first-eligible-check and reset rules for tool.custom_headless.skipped.
  The first readiness check finding the setting absent is eligible; an earlier configured check does not consume
  it. DS15 owns the prepared contract and applies this answer; DT drops its blocked row and cites DS15. Configuration
  edits, removal/re-addition and same-Project restores do not create a fresh notice; uncertain old backup evidence
  never justifies a duplicate.'
```

### DL-444 - The oldest eligible duplicate memory keeps its identity

```yaml
plan_unit_id: DL-444
unit_type: decision
status: accepted
owner_doc: Plans/Decision_Log.md
canonical_text: '**Card item:** E-CARDS-2 **6.a**. **Question:** Which eligible identical memory keeps its
  identity after a merge?


  Jared’s verbatim answer:


  > i approve all of it


  SourceRef: T3 thread 1338d738-7bb4-47b2-852e-38a876cb8521 (pm7-build), 2026-11-05T04:33:13Z, relayed to stream
  E by pm7-build (mail 1105043336-06d3). Answer file: `/mnt/Cursor/PuppetMaster-Evidence/event-authority-20261104/decision-answers/ANSWERS_E-CARDS-2_20261105.md`.
  Cards as presented: `/mnt/Cursor/PuppetMaster-Evidence/event-authority-20261104/decision-answers/E-CARDS-2.as-presented-6db25be3.md`,
  SHA-256 `6db25be3dd290ab0083af482383e469a78dc109a037ad0fd0ece5d8f15679b30`. Source aliases below are pinned
  by the presented deck’s Source revisions section.


  Coordinator pm7-build’s relayed reading (not Jared’s words): item **6.a** selects **A**. The presented deck’s
  fast-reply rule is: "`approve all` selects **A** on all 38 items."


  **Exact approved option text from the presented cards:**


  - **A (recommended):** Keep the oldest eligible memory by original creation time, breaking a tie by the unchanging
  note ID. Preserve every original evidence reference and the record of which copies were merged. If pin protection
  prevents that merge, skip it. You keep the earliest note ID and its history links.


  **Approved scope and conditions from the presented cards:**


  Deletion stays your action. Pins, versions, audit history and evidence references stay protected. A protected
  memory does not become mergeable through these choices. **6.a/6.b** govern duplicates; **6.c/6.d** govern
  separate archive jobs. The **usefulness score is a computed ranking, not a percentage of usefulness**. Its
  existing formula combines how strongly a memory matches keyword and meaning searches, how often/recently
  it was used, and its kind/status. Its contribution falls with age at the existing rate for that kind; Done
  memories lose weight faster. Each missing search score contributes zero. A pin protects the memory before
  scoring. Both age AND score must qualify, using values captured when the job chooses memories. A crowded
  list alone never triggers archiving. Automatic jobs and panel buttons stay unavailable until your answer
  is applied and all remaining definition, review and recording approvals pass.
```

```yaml
canonical_text: '**Card item:** E-CARDS-2 **6.d**. **Question:** Which age and usefulness-score cutoffs may
  prune/archive use?

  > i approve all of it

  fast-reply rule is: "`approve all` selects **A** on all 38 items."


  **Exact approved option text from the presented cards:**


  - **A (recommended):** Allow prune/archive to select eligible memories of any kind idle for at least 180
  days AND with usefulness score below 0.05. Apply the test separately inside each Project. If a chat outside
  a Project later receives its own fully specified and reviewed saved maintenance record and separate approval
  to record it, apply the test only inside that calling chat; never pool chats or Projects. Count idle days
  from the later of the last edit and last access, using creation time when either is absent. Use the existing
  computed usefulness ranking with inputs captured when the job chooses memories. Exclude pins before scoring.

  references and versions. Deletion remains your action. This cutoff choice supplies no separate permission
  to run outside a Project.


  **Approved scope and conditions from the presented cards:**


  Deletion stays your action. Pins, versions, audit history and evidence references stay protected. A protected
  memory does not become mergeable through these choices. **6.a/6.b** govern duplicates; **6.c/6.d** govern
  separate archive jobs. The **usefulness score is a computed ranking, not a percentage of usefulness**. Its
  existing formula combines how strongly a memory matches keyword and meaning searches, how often/recently
  it was used, and its kind/status. Its contribution falls with age at the existing rate for that kind; Done
  memories lose weight faster. Each missing search score contributes zero. A pin protects the memory before
  scoring. Both age AND score must qualify, using values captured when the job chooses memories. A crowded
  list alone never triggers archiving. Automatic jobs and panel buttons stay unavailable until your answer
```

```yaml
plan_unit_id: DL-454

owner_doc: Plans/Decision_Log.md
canonical_text: '**Card item:** E-CARDS-3 **2.a**. **Question:** Should these 33 routine histories stay for 90 days,
  seven years or permanently?


  Jared’s verbatim answer:


  > The rest I will defer to your recommendations.


  SourceRef: T3 thread 1338d738-7bb4-47b2-852e-38a876cb8521 (program thread pm7-build),
  2026-11-05T17:02:41Z, relayed to the stream E lead by pm7-build (mail 1105170345-d5f2). Answer

  E-CARDS-3.md.” Item **2.a** selects **A**. The presented deck’s fast-reply rule is: "`approve all`
  selects **A** on all twelve items."


  **Approved scope and conditions from the presented cards:**


  - **90 days:** counted from the entry''s first successful save that survives a restart. Retrying,
  reprocessing old history or restoring a backup never restarts it.


  - **Bounded counts:** Project entries share the existing **2,000,000 per Project** allowance for
  the selected seven-year or 90-day class. They get no fresh allowance per item. For a bounded
  option outside Projects, each item proposes **one separate 2,000,000-entry allowance**, shared by
  that item''s eligible types in one Puppet Master Server''s saved history, shared by its connected
  Clients. It is separate from every other item and all previously approved application allowances.
  Project-only names gain no outside-Project edition, and no entry is counted in both allowances.


  - **When a bounded allowance fills:** remove only expired entries with no legal/investigation
  hold, required recovery or source reference, rollback obligation or protected backup. Never drop
  unexpired entries to make room. If nothing eligible can free room, refuse new history writes. The
  underlying feature keeps its existing recording and safety requirements.


  For every option, protection for the latest 25 runs applies where the existing rule requires it.
  Holds and required references can keep history past its ordinary expiry; they grant no visibility
  or access. Existing Settings may lengthen an eligible history window, never shorten it below the
  chosen minimum. Original approvals, saved results, prompt text, documents, media and backup
  generations keep their own lifetimes.


  **Exact approved option text from the presented cards:**


  - **A (recommended):** Keep all 33 types for **90 days** from their first successful save that
  survives a restart, without resetting on retry, reprocessing or restore. Project entries share the
  existing 2,000,000-entry 90-day allowance. Approve one separate 2,000,000-entry application
  allowance for this item''s 29 application-eligible types. Delete only expired unprotected entries;
  refuse new writes if full and nothing may expire. You get recent history; older unprotected
  observations disappear.


  **Sources:** `S1307` (surveys/W3RT/QUESTIONS.md:75-124); `S1299`
  (decision-answers/E-CARDS-1.as-presented-578a6774.md:63-93); `S1269`
```

### DL-459 - Browser reader checkpoints keep a replaced copy seven days

```yaml
plan_unit_id: DL-459
unit_type: decision
status: accepted
owner_doc: Plans/Decision_Log.md
canonical_text: '**Card item:** E-CARDS-3 **6.b**. **Question:** How long should the two Browser history readers keep
  a replaced reader copy: seven days, 90 days or seven years?


  Jared’s verbatim answer:


  > The rest I will defer to your recommendations.


  SourceRef: T3 thread 1338d738-7bb4-47b2-852e-38a876cb8521 (program thread pm7-build),
  2026-11-05T17:02:41Z, relayed to the stream E lead by pm7-build (mail 1105170345-d5f2). Answer
  file:
  `/mnt/Cursor/PuppetMaster-Evidence/event-authority-20261104/decision-answers/ANSWERS_E-CARDS-3_20261105.md`.
  Cards as presented:
  `/mnt/Cursor/PuppetMaster-Evidence/event-authority-20261104/decision-answers/E-CARDS-3.as-presented-a7d00c73.md`,
  SHA-256 `a7d00c733539daa94b8a85bd9725d3658a4bbfcd7c1927507db0a4ace626db1f`. Source aliases below
  are the presented deck’s own S-aliases, resolved inline in each Sources line.


  Coordinator pm7-build’s relayed reading (not Jared’s words): “So A on all 12 items of
  E-CARDS-3.md.” Item **6.b** selects **A**. The presented deck’s fast-reply rule is: "`approve all`
  selects **A** on all twelve items."


  **Approved scope and conditions from the presented cards:**


  **Common boundary for all options:** keep the **current copy while that exact reader needs it**,
  with no age expiry while current. Keep at most **three copies together per reader, for one Project
  or for one Server''s history outside Projects**: the current copy plus any copies being built or
  replaced. The two readers have separate three-copy limits; no limit resets per source chat, and
  there is no 2,000,000-entry event allowance here. When a genuine replacement makes a new copy
  current, or the reader is withdrawn, the previously current copy''s clock starts at that moment;
  saving progress, retries and restores never start or restart it. Remove a replaced copy only when
  its chosen window has ended and it has no hold or required reference. A copy that was being built
  and was discarded without ever becoming current is removed through the existing authorized cleanup
  once it is shown never to have been used and its references and protections are cleared; it needs
  no window and no made-up retirement time. If all three copies must remain, refuse another build or
  replacement until a copy can lawfully be removed. An existing current copy may keep saving
  progress only while it still passes the reader''s checks against the retained original history. If
  the reader needs a rebuild to pass those checks, keep the last saved copy and show the affected
  reader as unavailable until a lawful rebuild is possible. A lost copy means checking retained
  original history again; it never recreates missing original events.


  Chat deletion still hides the deleted chat''s history immediately. Purge its unheld references
  from active reader copies within **24 hours** and backups within **30 days**; if a mixed copy
  cannot satisfy that by removing those references lawfully, discard the whole affected copy and
  rebuild only from retained, permitted original history. A missing complete source makes that
  reader unavailable, not permission to resurrect deleted history. Holds can delay physical purge
  without restoring access. Deleting the owning Project/app data follows its existing rules. These
  source-deletion limits override a copy''s remaining ordinary window; none of A/B/C lengthens an
  event, receipt, page or chat lifetime.


  **Exact approved option text from the presented cards:**


  - **A (recommended):** Keep a replaced copy for **seven days (604,800 seconds)** after it stops
  being current, under the common rules above. This follows the existing rule for disposable reader
  checkpoints. You keep a short recovery history; older unprotected copies are rebuilt when needed.


  **Sources:** `S1353` (8791f549ae15:Plans/Section15_MVP_Promoted_Features_Spec.md:13913-13920);
  `S1354` (8791f549ae15:Plans/Section15_MVP_Promoted_Features_Spec.md:13965-13972); `S1355`
  (57c28f706e10:Plans/storage-plan.md:19584-19605); `S1359`
  (57c28f706e10:Plans/storage_value_registry.json:175-190); `S1360`
  (57c28f706e10:Plans/storage-plan.md:20297-20330); `S1361`
  (57c28f706e10:Plans/storage-plan.md:21215-21221); `S1366`
  (9b76338594c6:Plans/storage-plan.md:17423-17425); `S1352` (drafts/DS15/DS15.md:92-103).


  **Supersession and boundaries:** Assigns the two Browser reader checkpoint keys a seven-day window
  for a replaced copy under the common three-copy boundary, with the current copy kept while its
  reader needs it. This is a saved-value rule, not an event allowance, and it extends no source
  event, receipt, page or chat lifetime.'
```

### DL-460 - Blocked-command history outside Projects gets its own allowance and scoped rule

```yaml
plan_unit_id: DL-460
unit_type: decision
status: accepted
owner_doc: Plans/Decision_Log.md
canonical_text: '**Card item:** E-CARDS-3 **7.a**. **Question:** Should blocked-command history outside Projects get
  its own 2,000,000-entry allowance and the scoped deletion/protection rule above?


  Jared’s verbatim answer:


  > The rest I will defer to your recommendations.


  SourceRef: T3 thread 1338d738-7bb4-47b2-852e-38a876cb8521 (program thread pm7-build),

  Cards as presented:
  `/mnt/Cursor/PuppetMaster-Evidence/event-authority-20261104/decision-answers/E-CARDS-3.as-presented-a7d00c73.md`,
  SHA-256 `a7d00c733539daa94b8a85bd9725d3658a4bbfcd7c1927507db0a4ace626db1f`. Source aliases below
  are the presented deck’s own S-aliases, resolved inline in each Sources line.


  Coordinator pm7-build’s relayed reading (not Jared’s words): “So A on all 12 items of
  E-CARDS-3.md.” Item **7.a** selects **A**. The presented deck’s fast-reply rule is: "`approve all`
  selects **A** on all twelve items."


  **Approved scope and conditions from the presented cards:**


  **What you already approved:** the second deck selected seven-year troubleshooting history for
  refused commands, guard-startup failures and refused paths; it selected permanent proof for
  refused destructive overrides and requests for those overrides. Its seven-year condition says
  “keep 2,555 days from the saved original refusal, override request or startup-failure result, up
  to 2,000,000 records per Project.” Its permanent condition says “no expiry by age or count” and
  preserves the entry after the described file or chat is deleted. Project proof is removed only by
  explicit **Delete Puppet Master project data** under the existing protections; **Remove project
  from list** retains it. At full storage, new entries are refused. These lifetimes and protections
  stay decided.


  **Proposed common boundary for A on each item:** count and store the named history in **one Puppet
  Master Server''s saved application history, shared by all its connected Clients**. No count resets
  per chat, Client, person, root, restart or workflow; a record belonging to a Project stays solely
  under its already approved Project rule. Shared counting grants no access to another person''s
  history or linked content. The three bounded A choices each propose their **own separate
  2,000,000-entry allowance** for that one type, separate from each other, the other items and every
  previously approved application allowance. The two permanent A choices have **no age or count
  limit**, as already chosen; imposing a 2,000,000-entry expiry on proof would reopen that answer.
  Every choice still obeys the Server''s existing finite disk budget, with no new byte limit or
  reserved disk allocation.


  **Proposed deletion and protection rule within each A:** ordinary file, chat or Project deletion,
  removing a Project from the list, disconnecting a Client, and history reaching capacity do not
  authorize deletion of this separate application history. Automatic expiry cleanup may remove only
  expired entries free of **every** legal/investigation hold, active source/reference, recovery,
  preserved/recent-run, rollback, maintenance and protected-backup obligation. Permanent proof has
  no automatic expiry cleanup.


  Earlier removal requires an **explicit, separately confirmed deletion request from a person
  authorized for that Server''s data**, naming that Server and this item''s exact FileSafe
  application history. Existing Storage ownership, permission, scope and destructive-intent checks
  must authorize it; a chat owner, a reference or a Project-delete request alone is insufficient.
  Persist the content-free deletion record and hide the selected history immediately; purge
  unprotected active copies within **24 hours** and backup bytes within **30 days**. The protections
  above preserve required custody until lawfully released, without restoring visibility or clearing
  a hold. Restore applies the deletion record before exposing history. If identity, permission,
  scope or protected references cannot be proved, refuse the deletion. This is a proposed
  authorization rule for the selected history, using the existing scoped Storage deletion mechanism;
  it grants no application-wide wipe permission or new delete control. Owners must bind that exact
  rule before recording. Original approvals, action results, snapshots, recovery journals and linked
  bodies keep their independent retention and access rules.


  **Exact approved option text from the presented cards:**


  - **A (recommended):** Give this one type of **blocked-command history its own 2,000,000-entry
  allowance outside Projects**, across the one Server and all connected Clients above. Keep the
  already chosen **2,555 days** from the saved original refusal or startup-failure result''s first
  successful save that survives a restart. Retry, reprocessing, restart recovery, restore and later
  observations never reset that original clock. Use this item''s proposed deletion/protection rule
  above. Only expired unprotected entries free ordinary capacity; never evict unexpired or protected
  entries to make room. If the count is full with no eligible expiry, or the existing disk budget
  prevents a safe save, refuse the new history entry. You get seven-year application troubleshooting
  history; expired unprotected entries can disappear, while ordinary file/chat/Project deletion does
  not shorten this separate history''s window. A separately authorized confirmed deletion follows
  the rule above.


  **Sources:** `S1276` (c81490e38cdd:Plans/Decision_Log.md:4880-4905); `S1377`
  (a10cfa6d834f:Plans/storage-plan.md:29528-29530); `S1370`
  (decision-answers/E-CARDS-2.as-presented-6db25be3.md:107-174); `S1388`
  (c81490e38cdd:Plans/Decision_Log.md:4784-4806); `S1382`
  (9b76338594c6:Plans/storage-plan.md:17491-17504); `S1375` (reviews/DF-sol/REVIEW-cycle7.md:71-99);
  `S1386` (57c28f706e10:Plans/storage-plan.md:17504-17516).


  **Supersession and boundaries:** Completes the outside-Project counting, capacity and
  authorized-deletion rule that DL-422 expressly reserved for filesafe.command_denied: its own
  2,000,000-entry Server-wide allowance under the already chosen 2,555-day clock and the scoped
  deletion/protection rule. The seven-year lifetime and Project rule are unchanged.'
```

### DL-054 - Parent List Truncates Only At The Bound And Expansion Echoes Currentness

```yaml
plan_unit_id: DL-054
unit_type: requirement
status: accepted
owner_doc: Plans/Decision_Log.md
canonical_text: >-
  Jared answered two review questions about the source graph parent-expansion contract on 2026-09-16
  with "1. no 2. yes 3. ok". A producer may not truncate a node's parent list before it holds all
  thirty-two references, so `parent_refs_truncated=true` always accompanies a full list and a shorter
  list always means the node has no further parents; the schema already enforced this and SCS-017 now
  states it. The parent-expansion request's `projection_currentness` echoes the page's `currentness`
  field for field, gaining the page's `expires_at_utc` as a required field that keeps the page's
  nullable shape, so the freshness horizon is readable from the request alone and the claim that the
  request is fenced exactly as page continuation is becomes literally true. The third answer accepts a
  whitespace-only re-indentation of the fixture entries this work added.
```
