### DL-259 - Onboarding Product Scope, Connectivity, Custody And Shared Help

```yaml
plan_unit_id: DL-259
unit_type: decision
status: accepted
owner_doc: Plans/Decision_Log.md
canonical_text: 'Jared 2026-10-31: canonical Plans specify real product behavior only; implementation illustrations and
  test-driving machinery belong outside product canon. This amendment removes this branch’s non-product additions while
  preserving the earlier baseline for the separately authorized Q3 cleanup. D1 A: the online-service step creates or
  selects a code repository; onboarding does not publish a website, GitHub Pages, GitLab Pages or another site. Local-only
  Project choices remain valid. D2 A: explicit always-on Server setup on this computer, manual private HTTPS, a self-hosted
  Remote Link gateway, rarer SSH key types, China-region AI variants and local AI servers live in Settings, with a clear
  context-correct pointer from onboarding. The ordinary This computer choice remains the easy local-work default. The
  wizard says AI accounts available in this setup, not every AI. Existing Settings routes and owners retain the advanced
  capabilities. D3 A: generated proxy settings support Caddy, NGINX and Traefik, with Caddy the default. Nginx Proxy
  Manager is existing-only: it can be selected as an existing proxy but never sent to a generation/install/export operation.
  DL-259 CERT-1 / srv C1, Jared 2026-10-31: onboarding offers Make the settings file or I have one already. The first
  generates/exports Caddy, NGINX or Traefik configuration for the person to add on their own system before the owner’s
  DNS, reachability and live-connection checks; Caddy is the default. The second only checks the existing proxy route
  and live connection, with nothing generated. Set it up for me is removed: Puppet Master does not install or host the
  proxy. The onboarding draft carries proxy_hosting=generate_only or existing_proxy for this new-Server proxy branch
  and keeps proxy_tls null; it collects no certificate choice. Generating a file proves neither installation nor consent,
  identity, secure reachability or a live route. For generation, onboarding proxy_kind is exactly caddy, nginx or traefik
  and maps to reverse_proxy_configuration.proxy_family. The existing-proxy branch may record nginx_proxy_manager but
  never emits a generated-configuration record; neither branch silently substitutes a family. D4: confirm provider admission
  and executable conformance immediately before building Puppet Master. The wizard lists its provider choices without
  unconfirmed/not-verified badges, warnings or caveats. This scheduling decision does not change per-account authentication,
  entitlement, health or quota truth: Ready is the shared account owner’s current usable result, not merely signed in.
  D5 A: the live Free Models source is github.com/vava-nessa/free-coding-models v0.6.0, read 2026-10-31; the June v0.5.39
  inspection remains historical lineage. Onboarding and Settings show OpenRouter free models (sign-in), Groq free plan
  (key) and NVIDIA free models (key) up front. Other currently eligible free providers from the same Free Models catalog
  appear behind one closed-by-default advanced control in each surface. That list is catalog-driven, never a pinned list
  or count, and still applies the Models owner’s supported/free/readiness filters. GitHub Models retired on 2026-07-30
  and has no active setup/catalog/routing action; saved choices remain No longer available and never become Copilot.
  Cerebras, Hugging Face and Ollama Cloud are excluded from the free offer. Authentication, billing class and currently
  usable account/model identity remain separate; catalog labels do not prove a route is free. No changing limits or prices
  are frozen in onboarding prose. D6 A: the human signs in on the initiating active device while the AI/tool runs on
  the selected execution host. Official tool sign-ins and private account roots stay with that tool on that host; direct
  API keys are held by Puppet Master’s secure credential store on that host. Onboarding, Settings, model selection and
  Usage share stable account/profile/host/environment references, never provider-name booleans or copied secrets. Protected
  returns are bound to the exact operation, initiating Client/session/generation and execution host. Changing account,
  host or route invalidates stale validation; another account of the same provider has a distinct identity. D7 B supersedes
  the former no-per-Client-node restriction. Native Puppet Master apps on Windows, macOS and Linux have their own built-in
  Tailscale connection and sign in once through the shared protected auth owner, with no separate Tailscale app install.
  The same signed PM-owned Go tsnet helper is supervised by its owning PM process. A Server keeps one active node per
  stable server_id; a native Client installation keeps one active node per stable client_id, independent of Projects,
  windows, tabs, sessions and Server endpoint selection. Owner-qualified configuration, process, IPC, authorization,
  egress and secure-state references prevent identity/key sharing or duplicate active nodes. Native Client nodes provide
  bounded Dial/stream access only to verified PM endpoints, not arbitrary proxying or a Server public listener. Server
  nodes retain the automatic private listener; Funnel remains Server-only, explicit, off by default and unavailable on
  Headscale. Human approval and reusable connection identity do not grant PM pairing/trust or work permission. A plain
  browser tab has no embedded Tailscale connection: it needs Remote Link or a private endpoint reachable through the
  device’s own Tailscale connection. It cannot be enrolled by a browser sign-in. Existing user-managed host Tailscale
  stays external and unmanaged. D8 A: onboarding has one FileSafe switch, default on, covering command blocklist, write
  scope, security filter and pre-write safe points together. Individual controls remain in Settings. The switch expresses
  a requested owner configuration, never approval to bypass a required guard, an absent allowlist/baseline, failed canonical-path
  resolution, failed initialization or failed safe-point persistence. Mandatory policy and effective guard state win;
  a refused change stays refused with a clear reason. No failure silently turns a guard off. ELI5: the wizard bar and
  Guided Tour bar expose the same global general.interaction.mode through the Settings owner, with values ELI5 and Expert,
  labels Plain English and Expert, and default ELI5. Both bars reflect the same effective state. Every opened onboarding
  question tip and prose help section has useful Plain English and technical versions, including FileSafe, service differences,
  storage, remote access and AI/auth choices, assuming no coding experience. Screen copy, control labels, exact fingerprints,
  paths and receipt data stay single; dual copy is limited to tips/help (DL-126). A mode change updates an open tip without
  rewriting a chat reply. Existing cmd.settings.transaction.preview/apply owns the preference; ui.guided_tour.toggle_eli5
  is a compatibility local adapter to that shared preference, not a tour-only setting or chat ELI5 command. The predecessor
  tour_narration_only tag is retired. Q1 B, Jared 2026-10-31: the shared Pip voice, say and vocals everywhere Pip speaks,
  sends 0.35 after trim and pan into its look’s room; Glass uses 0.30 and NieR 0.16. Each look uses its one per-look
  kit room, registered before the first shared voice in every host, with no stacked rooms. These restore the old voice’s
  own sends. Loudness remains within approximately 0.4 dB. The existing preference, gesture and sound owner still gates
  playback. Q2 A: Jared confirmed on 2026-10-31 that staged toasts stay below the open bell inbox through the existing
  --pmn-push; it is his ruling, not an unresolved lead exception. Closed-inbox theme-menu resting-top placement and entry/exit
  click guards remain. DL-259, Jared 2026-10-31: D2 A: onboarding offers NAS, Google Drive, OneDrive, Amazon S3, Backblaze
  B2, S3-compatible, SFTP and WebDAV backup choices, retaining their exact owner family/profile/locator identity. Azure
  Blob, Google Cloud Storage and REST-server destinations remain available in Settings > Backup & Restore, with a clear
  pointer. The Backup owner still supports all eleven registered families. D2 A: repository object-format selection and
  its permanence acknowledgement belong in Settings, not onboarding. Existing-repository format observation, unknown/capability
  handling and the Source Control owner’s safeguards remain unchanged. DL-259, Jared 2026-10-31, D4/D6: cursor_sdk is
  the separate Cursor SDK direct-provider entry, with API key as its default auth surface. A user key bills that user’s
  plan and a service-account key its owning team; these remain distinct account/billing identities. cursor_cli keeps
  browser login as its default and an advanced optional CLI-key path; it does not rename or absorb the SDK entry. alibaba_token_plan
  is a separate direct-provider entry for Alibaba Token Plan, a monthly-credit subscription with its own key and Singapore
  route identity, distinct from Alibaba Coding Plan and DashScope pay-as-you-go. MiniMax M Plan is the current label,
  with MiniMax Coding Plan retained as a former-name/search alias; OpenCode Console replaces the Zen display name and
  is a pay-as-you-go gateway. A label change never changes a saved provider/account ID. DL-259 D4, Jared 2026-10-31:
  immediately before PM is built, confirm Z.AI’s listed-tools rule, Kimi Code’s client/session identity, OpenCode Go’s
  client/session identity and Muse’s Muse-only subscription credential. This is the pre-build provider-conformance checklist,
  not a wizard warning, badge or disabled choice. DL-259 D6, Jared 2026-10-31: the Codex remote/headless device-code
  alternative requires enabling device-code login in ChatGPT security settings first, or the corresponding workspace
  permission by its administrator. This remains an alternative inside Sign in with ChatGPT, not another top-level auth
  family. DL-259 CERT-1, Jared 2026-10-31: Puppet Master generates the proxy configuration; the person handles certificates
  and signing on their own systems. PM does not select, hold, validate, issue or sign those certificates, and admits
  no certificate-profile field or selector command. No certificate selection/validation is a prerequisite to configuration
  generation, route activation or Ready. Generation proves only that the configuration artifact was produced. Route Ready
  reports the actual PM-owner checks performed: endpoint reachability, protocol/API compatibility, expected Server identity
  and pairing/auth, and the applicable WebSocket, stream, transfer, deep-link and callback checks. It never claims that
  a certificate is valid. Existing secure-transport, public-exposure consent, identity and reachability requirements
  remain; missing or failed actual route checks cannot be called successful. DL-259 CLOUD-1 A, Jared 2026-10-31: the
  person uses an explicit cloud-provider console or local-bootstrap handoff and its one-time Server setup code to claim
  a new cloud computer. The Server owner checks and consumes the code through the protected local/private bootstrap handoff.
  Its initial owner-claim authorization is bound to the existing discovery_observation_id, pairing_session_id and identity_fingerprint
  handed to cmd.server.claim, with the command’s current permission and generation fences. The tuple references owner-verified
  authority; guessed IDs, an address or a caller-provided success flag are not proof. Raw setup code never enters the
  ordinary command payload, stored setup plan, logs or receipts. No public unclaimed setup, automated provider-console/SSH
  provisioning or implicit tailnet enrollment is admitted. cmd.server.bootstrap.start remains separate after successful
  claim. DL-259 DESKTOP-RESTORE-1 A, Jared 2026-10-31: the native desktop performs the first owner claim of its dormant
  local Server through a protected direct local handoff, with no code for the person to type. The Server owner binds
  that initial owner-claim authorization to its discovery_observation_id, pairing_session_id and identity_fingerprint
  for the existing cmd.server.claim request and exact current permission/generations. Ordinary Clients, browser state
  and loopback reachability cannot manufacture this protected native authority. Claim then separate cmd.server.bootstrap.start
  must complete for the actual local Server, its durable roots/mounts and immutable execution baseline before cmd.restore.server_full.
  Backup maintenance/recovery authority, exact-target verification, paused restore and separate pairing/remote activation
  remain required. Reuse current verified prerequisites when already satisfied; dormant capability alone is never a claim
  or bootstrap receipt. DL-259 REMOTE-CODE-1 A, Jared 2026-10-31: the Remote Link owner issues and checks its protected
  HTTPS link or opaque short code. Decide the actual code grammar, normalization/case behavior, expiry/abuse policy and
  raw-code resolution protocol immediately before building PM, alongside D4’s pre-build checks; no grammar or sample
  code is pinned in canon. Preserve the owner-defined representation, reject empty input, and treat nonblank text as
  unverified draft rather than identity, pairing or Ready proof. After Review, the trusted owner validates/resolves it
  before the existing open and Server identity/pairing continuation. Unknown, expired or unresolvable input fails closed
  without another-Server fallback. This accepted pre-build verification point is not an unanswered product choice or
  a wizard caveat. DL-259 srv final, 2026-10-31: Creating observes only the reviewed Project creation/open/restore result
  and its actual prerequisites. It does not run optional remote-access configuration. After that owner settlement, a
  separate postcommit remote-setup view inside automatic_preparation runs any requested Remote Access continuation, before
  the normal provider/Free Models continuation; the eleven-stage graph is unchanged. Tailscale/Headscale authorization,
  new Remote Link output, and configuration-file/export or existing-proxy checks (CERT-1 / srv C1) use their existing
  domain owners, approvals and truthful results. Later always finishes onboarding and leaves the committed Project intact:
  it does not wait for optional setup, certify it, undo owner effects or invent readiness. Unstarted setup is deferred;
  any already-started work obeys the owner’s existing cancel/background rules, and the app shows its actual result or
  pending state. Existing whole-session ui.onboarding.skip/close semantics supply this exit without a new mutation command.
  DL-259 srv final, 2026-10-31: what the person actually set up is what the app shows. Enter/finish binds the shell,
  Settings and status views to the stable Client, Server, Execution Host, route and Project identities supplied by current
  owner results and registries, with their actual readiness/deferred state. Display names never become IDs, and the reviewed
  setup plan is intent rather than effective state. Onboarding creates no second account/server/Project registry or durable
  handoff writer; its initial context is a non-authoritative join of existing owner receipts/projections, followed by
  their normal updates. No concept-global object, event or store key is a product contract. Jared answered the four owner
  questions on 2026-10-31. CERT-1 is neither proposed selector option: his words are "Dont we just generate the proxy
  conf for them? They deal with signing and certs on their own systems." CLOUD-1 A selects the console one-time setup-code
  handoff. DESKTOP-RESTORE-1 A selects protected native local handoff with no typed code. REMOTE-CODE-1 A places protocol
  verification immediately before the product build. These decisions supersede the earlier tentative safeguards and close
  all four owner questions; the existing command IDs and typed claim tuple remain. Coverage-audit follow-up, 2026-10-31:
  accepted QA2 product rules include Auto retaining its mode while the Theme word follows the current family/OS scheme
  through the existing Settings writer; semantic technical-tooltip candidacy excluding internal container/render keys;
  focus-independent inner-overlay Escape; five equally prominent bounded look choices; readable settled-stage help notes
  without a separate tail; ordinary props visibly above the floor except Creating blocks; and No account yet retaining
  its category on return. Provider key rows use the exact official key console/guide through the existing protected official-page
  command and explain key versus password. Grouped First Project criteria, D7 shared consumers and five-family/ten-variant
  acceptance are reconciled in their owners. Concept API spellings move to source lineage under DL-260; they add no product
  request, persisted state or authority. Late integration amendment, 2026-10-31: automatic local Name previews never
  treat a placeholder/suggestion as a chosen folder; typed service addresses remain scoped to their service/variant;
  AI phase Skip immediately reveals its skipped-state feedback; and the online-copy/import view, Continue button and
  activation use one current choice/validation result, including the Protect/restore action-prerequisite sweep. These
  retain existing local actions, owner admission/commit and readiness truth. The GLM re-check at 17e87e52e0 closed all
  13 coverage findings; that static re-check is not native/runtime proof. DL-259 FO-4, 2026-10-31: onboarding provider
  rows and connected-account summaries show the category and concise product/account identity without billing explanations,
  prices, limits or extra-usage pitches. Retain useful category names and exact account/product distinctions; this presentation
  rule does not alter the provider owner’s charging model, auth surface, account identity or credential custody. DL-259
  FO-5, 2026-10-31: a choice’s question control stays visible, readable and reachable when its card is selected, hovered
  or keyboard-focused in every family. NieR’s selected/cursor ink stops before the help region or uses contrasting inverse
  ink there, without hiding the question, radio or selected state. DL-259 FO-6, 2026-10-31: a protected field keeps its
  typed value through redraws of the same screen and field identity, including typing in another field, opening help
  and changing Plain English/Expert. A blank rendering template alone must not erase it. The action clears the field
  when it consumes the input; leaving/recreating the screen, changing its service/method/target or explicit cancel/reset
  clears it too. Keep that input only in the protected entry control until consumption, never in ordinary draft/session
  persistence, receipts or logs. A filled/masked flag is not a credential or validation proof; submission reads the current
  protected value and rechecks its existing owner requirements. DL-259 FO-7, 2026-10-31: accepting an owner’s approval
  or rejection finishes that exact pairing request/generation in the view. Clear its obsolete warning and render the
  answered result; later refreshes must not re-adopt the consumed result as a new request or show a false used-answer
  warning. The answered view offers a fresh code/request rather than Check again for the completed one. A fresh invitation
  starts a new generation; exact Server/Client/session/generation, matching-identity confirmation, permission, expiry
  and genuine replay rejection remain. Rejecting a later request cannot remove a Client already approved by an earlier
  request. A view marker never grants trust or bypasses the Server owner. DL-259 FO-8, 2026-10-31: after actual clipboard
  success, Copy’s transient Copied acknowledgment holds for its full feedback interval across redraws of that same control,
  including countdown updates. Another successful copy starts a fresh full interval; an older timeout cannot clear its
  newer acknowledgment. Failure reports no success. Feedback is local presentation state and does not retain the copied
  protected value or become a saved preference, owner receipt or proof of any other operation. DL-259 FO-9 final, 2026-10-31:
  Creating’s checklist and block stack share the accepted owner’s phase/effect projection. When GitHub creation only
  partly settles, show only verified completed phases as checked or landed blocks; the phase proven to have failed may
  show failure and unexecuted/unproven phases remain pending. Unexecuted or unproven phases stay pending through an incomplete
  or unclear result until a later accepted owner result from Continue Setup or Check again proves those effects settled.
  The checklist, stage block count and stage progress use that same result; a settled phase keeps its block and an unproven
  phase has no completed block. Refresh alone neither completes a phase nor repeats a settled remote create. Transport
  completion and animation never prove the later registration, settings or connection steps. The recovery banner/actions,
  Continue availability and Ready use that same current owner result; O12’s last-block landing condition is additional
  to owner completion, never a replacement for it. DL-259 FS-1, 2026-10-31, supersedes Q17’s dimming: hover/focus emphasis
  begins only at an actual control in its affects region, including an embedded plate control; plain text, empty space
  and the picture alone trigger none. Affected marks take a one-pixel theme accent ring, with the shared soft glow in
  Glass and ink in NieR; their connecting lines and the job-card edge take accent, and the linked read-back takes the
  shared wash. Hover/focus never lowers another cast part’s opacity or recolours a Pip body, seat or label; each retains
  its intrinsic colours. Genuine owner-state quietness remains independent of hover. Scheduled emphasises only a row/mark
  with a drawn partner and never dims unrelated marks. Keyboard focus uses the same emphasis, Reduced Motion settles
  it instantly, and emphasis changes no layout or owner state. One shared affects/partner owner serves every sheet; there
  is no per-sheet hover engine. DL-259 FS-2 / plate text, 2026-10-31: the input paper’s fixed label and supporting fixed
  words (including The job and Your latest changes) fit their actual inner text box in each family, counting its padding/insets
  before sizing or fitting text. User-supplied job text retains the existing bounded fit. BrainStorm’s final chapter
  name keeps a visible gap from You after all placement offsets; labels never run together. Preserve the richest-mode-that-fits
  and no-scale/no-scroll yield rules: compact means names only and intentionally omits model lines, including Retro;
  full mode retains its model line. This adds no new plate mode, glyph, status or model-selection behavior. DL-259 FX-1
  final, 2026-10-31: an export/print attempt that fails before producing a PDF closes any unusable temporary print window
  and says plainly in its result/receipt and visible failure notice that no PDF was made. Opening the print flow alone
  is not proof that a file was created. A receipt records only the artifact owner’s actual result and never claims a
  successful PDF that was not made; failure or cancellation leaves the exact Plan revision unchanged. This is an outcome/feedback
  rule, not a new export command, receipt family or platform-detection mechanism. DL-259 FO-10 final, 2026-10-31: on
  Connect’s route screen, disabled Continue gives an actionable reason for the selected route’s visible input before
  an unresolved Server-choice reason. Web address and Remote Link use that field’s current missing/invalid-address result;
  an address typed instead of the found list asks for the address when empty and explains when no Puppet Master answers,
  with a route back to the list. Say Choose your Puppet Master only while the found-Server choice list is shown. Pip’s
  feedback conveys the same cause. These screen/status words stay single in Plain English and Expert (DL-126); only tips/help
  have two versions. Reason priority changes no validation, route identity, readiness, pairing or permission gate and
  admits no address/Remote Link grammar.'
gui_related: true
gui_classification_reason: Sets actual onboarding choices, shared explanation controls, native connection setup and Pip/notice
  presentation.
split_recommended: false
depends_on:
- PWIZ-021
- PWIZ-022
- PWIZ-025
- RAS-005
- RAS-014
- RAS-015
- MS-118
- F2-030
- DL-257
unblocks: []
acceptance_criteria:
- 'D1 A: the online-service step creates or selects a code repository; onboarding does not publish a website, GitHub
  Pages, GitLab Pages or another site. Local-only Project choices remain valid.'
- 'D2 A: explicit always-on Server setup on this computer, manual private HTTPS, a self-hosted Remote Link gateway, rarer
  SSH key types, China-region AI variants and local AI servers live in Settings, with a clear context-correct pointer
  from onboarding. The ordinary This computer choice remains the easy local-work default. The wizard says AI accounts
  available in this setup, not every AI. Existing Settings routes and owners retain the advanced capabilities.'
- 'D3 A: generated proxy settings support Caddy, NGINX and Traefik, with Caddy the default. Nginx Proxy Manager is existing-only:
  it can be selected as an existing proxy but never sent to a generation/install/export operation. DL-259 CERT-1 / srv
  C1, Jared 2026-10-31: onboarding offers Make the settings file or I have one already. The first generates/exports Caddy,
  NGINX or Traefik configuration for the person to add on their own system before the owner’s DNS, reachability and live-connection
  checks; Caddy is the default. The second only checks the existing proxy route and live connection, with nothing generated.
  Set it up for me is removed: Puppet Master does not install or host the proxy. The onboarding draft carries proxy_hosting=generate_only
  or existing_proxy for this new-Server proxy branch and keeps proxy_tls null; it collects no certificate choice. Generating
  a file proves neither installation nor consent, identity, secure reachability or a live route. For generation, onboarding
  proxy_kind is exactly caddy, nginx or traefik and maps to reverse_proxy_configuration.proxy_family. The existing-proxy
  branch may record nginx_proxy_manager but never emits a generated-configuration record; neither branch silently substitutes
  a family.'
- 'D4: confirm provider admission and executable conformance immediately before building Puppet Master. The wizard lists
  its provider choices without unconfirmed/not-verified badges, warnings or caveats. This scheduling decision does not
  change per-account authentication, entitlement, health or quota truth: Ready is the shared account owner’s current
  usable result, not merely signed in.'
- 'D5 A: the live Free Models source is github.com/vava-nessa/free-coding-models v0.6.0, read 2026-10-31; the June v0.5.39
  inspection remains historical lineage. Onboarding and Settings show OpenRouter free models (sign-in), Groq free plan
  (key) and NVIDIA free models (key) up front. Other currently eligible free providers from the same Free Models catalog
  appear behind one closed-by-default advanced control in each surface. That list is catalog-driven, never a pinned list
  or count, and still applies the Models owner’s supported/free/readiness filters. GitHub Models retired on 2026-07-30
  and has no active setup/catalog/routing action; saved choices remain No longer available and never become Copilot.
  Cerebras, Hugging Face and Ollama Cloud are excluded from the free offer. Authentication, billing class and currently
  usable account/model identity remain separate; catalog labels do not prove a route is free. No changing limits or prices
  are frozen in onboarding prose.'
- 'D6 A: the human signs in on the initiating active device while the AI/tool runs on the selected execution host. Official
  tool sign-ins and private account roots stay with that tool on that host; direct API keys are held by Puppet Master’s
  secure credential store on that host. Onboarding, Settings, model selection and Usage share stable account/profile/host/environment
  references, never provider-name booleans or copied secrets. Protected returns are bound to the exact operation, initiating
  Client/session/generation and execution host. Changing account, host or route invalidates stale validation; another
  account of the same provider has a distinct identity.'
- 'D7 B supersedes the former no-per-Client-node restriction. Native Puppet Master apps on Windows, macOS and Linux have
  their own built-in Tailscale connection and sign in once through the shared protected auth owner, with no separate
  Tailscale app install. The same signed PM-owned Go tsnet helper is supervised by its owning PM process. A Server keeps
  one active node per stable server_id; a native Client installation keeps one active node per stable client_id, independent
  of Projects, windows, tabs, sessions and Server endpoint selection. Owner-qualified configuration, process, IPC, authorization,
  egress and secure-state references prevent identity/key sharing or duplicate active nodes. Native Client nodes provide
  bounded Dial/stream access only to verified PM endpoints, not arbitrary proxying or a Server public listener. Server
  nodes retain the automatic private listener; Funnel remains Server-only, explicit, off by default and unavailable on
  Headscale. Human approval and reusable connection identity do not grant PM pairing/trust or work permission. A plain
  browser tab has no embedded Tailscale connection: it needs Remote Link or a private endpoint reachable through the
  device’s own Tailscale connection. It cannot be enrolled by a browser sign-in. Existing user-managed host Tailscale
  stays external and unmanaged.'
- 'D8 A: onboarding has one FileSafe switch, default on, covering command blocklist, write scope, security filter and
  pre-write safe points together. Individual controls remain in Settings. The switch expresses a requested owner configuration,
  never approval to bypass a required guard, an absent allowlist/baseline, failed canonical-path resolution, failed initialization
  or failed safe-point persistence. Mandatory policy and effective guard state win; a refused change stays refused with
  a clear reason. No failure silently turns a guard off.'
- 'ELI5: the wizard bar and Guided Tour bar expose the same global general.interaction.mode through the Settings owner,
  with values ELI5 and Expert, labels Plain English and Expert, and default ELI5. Both bars reflect the same effective
  state. Every opened onboarding question tip and prose help section has useful Plain English and technical versions,
  including FileSafe, service differences, storage, remote access and AI/auth choices, assuming no coding experience.
  Screen copy, control labels, exact fingerprints, paths and receipt data stay single; dual copy is limited to tips/help
  (DL-126). A mode change updates an open tip without rewriting a chat reply. Existing cmd.settings.transaction.preview/apply
  owns the preference; ui.guided_tour.toggle_eli5 is a compatibility local adapter to that shared preference, not a tour-only
  setting or chat ELI5 command. The predecessor tour_narration_only tag is retired.'
- 'Q1 B, Jared 2026-10-31: the shared Pip voice, say and vocals everywhere Pip speaks, sends 0.35 after trim and pan
  into its look’s room; Glass uses 0.30 and NieR 0.16. Each look uses its one per-look kit room, registered before the
  first shared voice in every host, with no stacked rooms. These restore the old voice’s own sends. Loudness remains
  within approximately 0.4 dB. The existing preference, gesture and sound owner still gates playback.'
- 'Q2 A: Jared confirmed on 2026-10-31 that staged toasts stay below the open bell inbox through the existing --pmn-push;
  it is his ruling, not an unresolved lead exception. Closed-inbox theme-menu resting-top placement and entry/exit click
  guards remain.'
- 'D2 A: onboarding offers NAS, Google Drive, OneDrive, Amazon S3, Backblaze B2, S3-compatible, SFTP and WebDAV backup
  choices, retaining their exact owner family/profile/locator identity. Azure Blob, Google Cloud Storage and REST-server
  destinations remain available in Settings > Backup & Restore, with a clear pointer. The Backup owner still supports
  all eleven registered families.'
- 'D2 A: repository object-format selection and its permanence acknowledgement belong in Settings, not onboarding. Existing-repository
  format observation, unknown/capability handling and the Source Control owner’s safeguards remain unchanged.'
- 'DL-259, Jared 2026-10-31, D4/D6: cursor_sdk is the separate Cursor SDK direct-provider entry, with API key as its
  default auth surface. A user key bills that user’s plan and a service-account key its owning team; these remain distinct
  account/billing identities. cursor_cli keeps browser login as its default and an advanced optional CLI-key path; it
  does not rename or absorb the SDK entry. alibaba_token_plan is a separate direct-provider entry for Alibaba Token Plan,
  a monthly-credit subscription with its own key and Singapore route identity, distinct from Alibaba Coding Plan and
  DashScope pay-as-you-go. MiniMax M Plan is the current label, with MiniMax Coding Plan retained as a former-name/search
  alias; OpenCode Console replaces the Zen display name and is a pay-as-you-go gateway. A label change never changes
  a saved provider/account ID.'
- 'DL-259 D4, Jared 2026-10-31: immediately before PM is built, confirm Z.AI’s listed-tools rule, Kimi Code’s client/session
  identity, OpenCode Go’s client/session identity and Muse’s Muse-only subscription credential. This is the pre-build
  provider-conformance checklist, not a wizard warning, badge or disabled choice.'
- 'DL-259 D6, Jared 2026-10-31: the Codex remote/headless device-code alternative requires enabling device-code login
  in ChatGPT security settings first, or the corresponding workspace permission by its administrator. This remains an
  alternative inside Sign in with ChatGPT, not another top-level auth family.'
- 'DL-259 CERT-1, Jared 2026-10-31: Puppet Master generates the proxy configuration; the person handles certificates
  and signing on their own systems. PM does not select, hold, validate, issue or sign those certificates, and admits
  no certificate-profile field or selector command. No certificate selection/validation is a prerequisite to configuration
  generation, route activation or Ready. Generation proves only that the configuration artifact was produced. Route Ready
  reports the actual PM-owner checks performed: endpoint reachability, protocol/API compatibility, expected Server identity
  and pairing/auth, and the applicable WebSocket, stream, transfer, deep-link and callback checks. It never claims that
  a certificate is valid. Existing secure-transport, public-exposure consent, identity and reachability requirements
  remain; missing or failed actual route checks cannot be called successful.'

  nor repeats a settled remote create. Transport completion and animation never prove the later registration, settings
  or connection steps. The recovery banner/actions, Continue availability and Ready use that same current owner result;
  O12’s last-block landing condition is additional to owner completion, never a replacement for it. DL-259 FS-1, 2026-10-31,
  supersedes Q17’s dimming: hover/focus emphasis begins only at an actual control in its affects region, including an
  embedded plate control; plain text, empty space and the picture alone trigger none. Affected marks take a one-pixel
  theme accent ring, with the shared soft glow in Glass and ink in NieR; their connecting lines and the job-card edge
  take accent, and the linked read-back takes the shared wash. Hover/focus never lowers another cast part’s opacity or
  recolours a Pip body, seat or label; each retains its intrinsic colours. Genuine owner-state quietness remains independent
  of hover. Scheduled emphasises only a row/mark with a drawn partner and never dims unrelated marks. Keyboard focus
  uses the same emphasis, Reduced Motion settles it instantly, and emphasis changes no layout or owner state. One shared
  affects/partner owner serves every sheet; there is no per-sheet hover engine. DL-259 FS-2 / plate text, 2026-10-31:
  the input paper’s fixed label and supporting fixed words (including The job and Your latest changes) fit their actual
  inner text box in each family, counting its padding/insets before sizing or fitting text. User-supplied job text retains
  the existing bounded fit. BrainStorm’s final chapter name keeps a visible gap from You after all placement offsets;
  labels never run together. Preserve the richest-mode-that-fits and no-scale/no-scroll yield rules: compact means names
  only and intentionally omits model lines, including Retro; full mode retains its model line. This adds no new plate
  mode, glyph, status or model-selection behavior. DL-259 FX-1 product portion, 2026-10-31: editing a terminal’s name
  stays in its own tab context menu, with Rename/Enter accepting the changed label and Cancel/Escape leaving it unchanged.
  Use the existing cmd.panel_tab.rename once; clearing the label still restores the terminal’s own name. DL-181’s retirement
  of workgroups and their commands remains in force. DL-259 FX-1 product portion, 2026-10-31: PDF export/print feedback
  names what actually happened. Opening the print flow is not proof that a PDF was written. If export or printing is
  unavailable, blocked or fails before producing a file, say plainly that no PDF was made and keep the exact Plan revision
  unchanged. The existing artifact owner’s verified result is the only success evidence; cancellation and failure cannot
  produce a successful export receipt.'
- 'DL-259 FX-1 final, 2026-10-31: an export/print attempt that fails before producing a PDF closes any unusable temporary
  print window and says plainly in its result/receipt and visible failure notice that no PDF was made. Opening the print
  flow alone is not proof that a file was created. A receipt records only the artifact owner’s actual result and never
  claims a successful PDF that was not made; failure or cancellation leaves the exact Plan revision unchanged. This is
  an outcome/feedback rule, not a new export command, receipt family or platform-detection mechanism.'
- 'DL-259 FO-10 final, 2026-10-31: on Connect’s route screen, disabled Continue gives an actionable reason for the selected
  route’s visible input before an unresolved Server-choice reason. Web address and Remote Link use that field’s current
  missing/invalid-address result; an address typed instead of the found list asks for the address when empty and explains
  when no Puppet Master answers, with a route back to the list. Say Choose your Puppet Master only while the found-Server
  choice list is shown. Pip’s feedback conveys the same cause. These screen/status words stay single in Plain English
  and Expert (DL-126); only tips/help have two versions. Reason priority changes no validation, route identity, readiness,
  pairing or permission gate and admits no address/Remote Link grammar.'

```yaml
plan_unit_id: DL-260

  canon, including material inherited from main before this build. The test is whether the behavior exists in the real
  product. Prototypes, sample loaders, prefilled choices, lab-only controls, clocks, fixture workspaces, hidden demo
  bridges, concept-page persistence and runtime admission for simulated receipts are not product requirements, commands,
  Settings, wiring, registries, schemas, fixtures or implementation debt. Concept source files remain untouched as design/source
  history. Historical decisions remain unchanged: this entry supersedes only the Demo Studio/concept-mechanics portions
  of DL-106, DL-144, DL-177, DL-185, DL-212, DL-227, DL-230, DL-232, DL-233 and DL-234. Their real product decisions
  remain in force. F3-649, ACD-474 and DR-070 retain retired identifiers solely so those historical links resolve, with
  no active requirement or work compilation. The guided tour remains a real feature under PWIZ-023/035/036 and F3-521;
  shared Settings, Usage Live/Pause, tab routing, work status, Pip sound and appearance, and all other genuine behavior
  stay with their production owners. Real motion follows the theme family, no fixture creates completion or Ready, and

### DL-270 - Storage Review Decisions: Compression, Durability, Payloads, Pages, Mirrors, Analytics, Engines, Media, Gates

```yaml
plan_unit_id: DL-270
unit_type: decision
status: accepted
owner_doc: Plans/Decision_Log.md
canonical_text: >-
  Recorded 2026-10-31. On 2026-10-30 Jared asked for a review of PM's database, log, cache and compression plans
  against current competitors and engines, by Fable 5.1, GPT-6 Astra, Muse Wonder and Opus 5.5, and then for the
  review's unverified items to be tested on the VM, his MacBook Air and his Windows PC. The packet, ten reports
  and four test reports are in /mnt/Cursor/share/puppet-master/2026-10-30-storage-compression-review/. Between
  18:50Z and 19:04Z on 2026-10-31 he answered all 13 decision cards and chose the recommended option on each: 1,
  "Compress the event log": "Compress closed segments; format ready now"; 2, "Save each batch with one disk sync,
  not four": "One sync per batch; full flush for key moments"; 3, "Store big tool output and images once": "Store
  once by fingerprint, reference everywhere"; 4, "Open any chat instantly, however long": "Ready-made pages plus a
  speed test"; 5, "Drop the JSON copies; add dump and inspect commands": "Copies off; readable on demand"; 6,
  "Keep redb lean and reclaim its space": "Size limits, two files, scheduled compaction"; 7, "Add SQL over your
  own history": "Parquet archives plus DuckDB on demand"; 8, "Back up without freezing PM": "Background copy plus
  a shown loss window"; 9, "Keep the SQLite ban, written as your four requirements": "Ban plus your four
  requirements plus narrow exceptions"; 10, "Compress remote access with zstd streams": "zstd stream with a
  fallback"; 11, "Store screenshots as lossless WebP": "Lossless WebP in the background; evidence keeps
  originals"; 12, "Turn your four requirements into pass/fail tests": "Gate every release on all three OSes"; 13,
  "Keep Spotlight, Windows Search and Defender off PM's data": "Put data where indexers don't look, in few files".
  On card 7 he added, verbatim: "Do we need to tie the usage data to this?  In my work on AAC, the usage data
  takes a long time to load and doesn’t keep its data, I know there is a lot of data there so just want to make
  sure that is accounted for." The reply he received, that usage loads from rollups and that usage history and
  daily totals are kept, is adopted as refined by his follow-up answer the same evening on the Keep usage history
  for setting, verbatim: "Defualt to 90 days, selectable to longer or shorter time periods." So
  ai.usage.usage-retention stays as it is, 90 days by default, and governs detailed usage records, while daily
  usage totals are kept whatever it says. His reasons for the SQLite ban, 2026-10-30, verbatim: "I banned sqlite
  because it is slow, has serious contention and lock issues, and I have seen them corrupt frequently. I have used
  so many programs that have been completely ruined because they use sqlite. For example, plex is very very held
  back by its DB." On JSON files, 2026-10-30, verbatim: "We also should likely not be using a bunch of json files,
  that seems worse than a well structured DB." Owners: SP-335 to SP-345 in Plans/storage-plan.md for the storage
  rules; ACD-242 for mandatory load-older paging; UF-108 for usage history; BRS-031 for backup capture; RAS-016
  for remote transport. Where earlier text conflicts, DL-270 and those units win. A sweep of every plan document
  by a reading wave, with verification, brought the other owners into line in the same landing, including the
  commands, settings, GUI, wiring and DRY companions. DL-270 adds no settings row: budgets, thresholds and cache
  sizes are fixed owner values, while Jared reconsiders how settings are scoped. Its companions landed after it:
  SP-346 for SeglogFrameV2's reserved compression descriptor and the sealed segment container, SP-347 for the
  commit frame and its receipt fields, the First append receipt custody section and CV-339 rewritten to SP-336's
  publication and recovery sequence, the data-root paths in SP-015, and the storage registry's storage_profile
  with its schema, holding each family's file, group and value limit and the budget values. The companion audits
  left three items for implementation, not planning: a producer-valid fixture that rebuilds complete custody rows
  from frames; native crash, power-loss and recovery tests of the commit-frame sequence on all three operating
  systems; and recertifying the pinned goal_certified_event_coordinator_contracts profile against SP-336 before
  its route is enabled. Only the governance reseal remains outside it. Card 4's 150 ms applies to warm and cold
  opens alike. Spec_Lock's forbid_sqlite is unchanged. The option labels are the cards' words; the four
  requirements, thresholds and mechanics are the review's reading, not Jared's words.
gui_related: false
gui_classification_reason: "Records owner decisions on storage, compression and durability."
split_recommended: false

  - "Spec_Lock, .evidence and auto_decisions are unchanged."

## DL-271 — Onboarding credential, recovery and pairing feedback

```yaml
plan_unit_id: DL-271
unit_type: decision_record
status: accepted
owner_doc: Plans/Decision_Log.md
canonical_text: 'DL-271 records the PM7 final onboarding batch accepted through the lead on 2026-10-31. DL-271 FO-11,
  2026-10-31: where an OpenCode server requires its own HTTP Basic credentials, the Password field asks for that server’s
  password, not an AI provider’s API key or the person’s Puppet Master sign-in. Its hint states that distinction and
  identifies credential custody in the OS keychain on the selected execution host, through the existing credential owner.
  Optional server auth stays optional when the server needs none. Protected entry, secret-free readback and exact host/account
  binding remain; an API-key-only hint is used only on an actual API-key field. DL-271 FO-12, 2026-10-31: Protect’s missing-access
  guidance is count-neutral: ask for the access details without claiming a fixed number of fields. The selected Backup
  destination family, auth method and credential mode determine the actual required fields and validation through their
  existing owner. Changing the line never omits a required credential, locator, region or temporary-session value and
  never turns incomplete access into an available Connect action. DL-271 Unlock wording, 2026-10-31: ask for your recovery
  phrase, rather than six words or another fixed word count. The Recovery Kit is not a six-word format (PWIZ-025/BRS-018);
  the Backup owner still defines and verifies the real protected recovery material and its exact source/target binding.
  The wording admits no new phrase format, key derivation, unlock proof or weaker secret-handling rule. DL-271 weak-key
  eligibility, 2026-10-31: Choose a key may list a DSA or RSA-1024 key as Too weak to use, but it cannot be selected,
  used as a default, advanced or installed. The refusal reads Older key type — too weak to use. Check this eligibility
  before an existing authorization, matching prior profile or passphrase/unlock state; those cannot make a weak key usable.
  A retained weak selection must be replaced by an owner-eligible key before the flow advances. Other keys keep their
  existing owner checks, identity binding and custody; the shared list never exposes or moves a private half. DL-271
  initial request waiting, 2026-10-31: while the current invitation is live and no device request has arrived, Your Server
  is ready shows No requests yet with Check again. Checking re-reads the current owner run; a real arriving request also
  updates that view. This neutral state is not an error and invents no candidate, approval or trust. Continue retains
  its existing Server-ready gates. Keep it distinct from DL-259 FO-7’s answered approval/rejection: a completed request
  stays answered, and a fresh request requires the existing new-code/new-generation route. DL-271 FO-14, 2026-10-31:
  long tokens in an opened question note wrap within its available width, so their full text is readable without horizontal
  scrolling. Keep vertical scrolling when the note exceeds its available height. This applies to Plain English and Expert,
  including NieR, and visual wrapping preserves the exact token for copying; it adds no second note renderer or per-family
  content version.'

Unknown/custom protective combinations use the owner's declared fallback, not an invented ordering. SSYS-002/059 owns classification and resolution. This supersedes the universal Project-only persistence and inheritance bans, resolves q-035 in favor of a real ordinary Everywhere store, and leaves source-memory ledgers unchanged.

### DL-282 - One Settings Home And Explicit Joining

```yaml
plan_unit_id: DL-282
unit_type: decision_record
status: accepted
owner_doc: Plans/Decision_Log.md
canonical_text: |-
  S7 and S12 are accepted. One Computer keeps the shared settings and other same-owner Computers follow it through explicit protected trust. Each level has one writer and bounded read-only mirrors or caches. A Computer that cannot reach the writer may show the last known values with their age; it cannot queue edits, elect itself writer or silently fail over. Joining two existing setups first chooses the home and shows exact differences, alternatives and affected contexts. The accepted join Undo lasts 30 days. Ordinary per-setting Undo keeps its existing owner policy.

  Home transfer verifies the copy and history, fences the old writer and switches the role generation once. A stale copy acknowledgement cannot prove the old writer is fenced; recovery without that proof remains blocked. Settings following never grants access to Projects, files, chats or another person's work. SSYS-060 and SRV-016 own these rules, with storage binding them rather than creating another synchronization engine.

### DL-291 - Two Equal Ways To Join A Project With Report And Undo

```yaml
plan_unit_id: DL-291
unit_type: decision_record
status: accepted
owner_doc: Plans/Decision_Log.md
canonical_text: |-
  N2, N9, N11, N13, N20, N25 and N27 and Q1/Q2 are accepted. Make a project from this chat and Move this chat into a project are equal first-class choices, neither preselected. Each names what will happen, shows a fresh preview, acts through a button naming the action, then reports moved/stayed/held/failed work and offers Undo. Moving into an existing Project defaults to a separate branch/worktree or admitted Jujutsu change/bookmark and a chosen folder; direct main is Advanced. Keep-both is the conflict default; unsaved work is never overwritten.

  A new Project is committed/listed first. Files copy and verify before the single live writer cuts over, including across Computers. The retained thread ID gets full destination-owned history; original immutable events, usage and receipts stay sealed with lineage and no re-charge. Goal, Crew and Plan default to linked new destination records; only a complete separate owner rebind may change association. Active work is stopped/fenced and exact future schedules are held and explicitly re-admitted with fresh target authority, never silently retargeted or dispatched twice.

  Undo ends at first new work or seven days. It never deletes remote repositories, branches, backups, changed work or independently retained canonical/audit custody. Regular applies by the person; N27 admits the guarded YOLO owner route only when the task clearly asks for a new Project or names the existing destination. Ambiguous convert this still asks for a destination. Merge means a chat joining a Project, not two chats; moving Project chats between Projects comes later.

### DL-299 - Approve A Build Grant Once And Show Every Target

```yaml
plan_unit_id: DL-299

status: accepted

The person approves one exact Plan-bound build grant listing needed operations and resources: repository create/push, publication namespaces, CI setup/execution and deployment targets. The Orchestrator and narrower children then run YOLO within that grant, without repeating those ordinary prompts. A changed Plan, target, permission ceiling or Stop/revocation generation never silently widens it; no agent issues, expands or renews its own grant.

  A verified created-resource manifest binds stable IDs/generations and ownership receipts. The build may change or clean up what this grant demonstrably created, within the enumerated operations. Naming a pre-existing resource does not grant deletion, a name prefix is not ownership and a namespace does not authorize every child object. This is the narrow grant exception to Y1's ordinary risky-action asks, never permission to force-push main, touch unrelated resources or bypass FileSafe/trust/secrets. Secrets, paid sign-ups and protected administration retain their separate human choices.

  What the build did reads the existing work/History projection and lists each remote action, exact target, authority and outcome, including pending, blocked or unknown. One run-owner Stop fences new dispatch and children. Undo is offered only where safe; otherwise say No safe Undo. Existing final YOLO checks remain. App Goals/Crew and cross-project requests cannot borrow this Project's grant.

### DL-341 - Command Definitions Record Judgments, And UCC-230 Gains Nullable Fields, Canon Enum Spelling, Identity Aliases And The Chat-Tool Approval Branch

```yaml
plan_unit_id: DL-341
unit_type: decision
status: accepted
owner_doc: Plans/Decision_Log.md
canonical_text: >-
  DL-341 amends the pm.command_payload_definitions.v1 format and the UCC-230 map in Plans/UI_Command_Catalog.md
  after rounds 1 to 3 of the blind review of the 275 Q5 command payload definitions (DL-333). In round 1 all five
  review slices failed (3 blockers, 27 majors, 42 minors) while scripts/pm-command-payload-defs-check.py passed.
  Part of the cause was the format and the map: writers had nowhere to record a judgment except a YAML comment,
  which no tool reads, the vocabulary had no nullable form and forced snake_case enum values, and the map missed
  aliases and rules that canon states. Format: a definition records each judgment it makes in an optional judgments
  list of key, choice and gap_note entries. The key is command_kind, response_kind, disabled_reason_codes,
  error_codes, owner_request, owner_result, aliases, omitted:<field> for a field it deliberately leaves out, or
  field:<arg path>; the choice is what the definition chose, equal to its own value for a fixed key; the gap_note
  says what canon lacks or where it disagrees. A judgment carries no provenance, a canon field whose source or
  gap_note says JUDGMENT is a provenance finding, and reviewers check judgments as they check fields. A definitions
  block holds no YAML comment, whatever it says, and no string that names review or evidence material. A field
  marked nullable: true may be JSON null, with any required value, except a required row-group identity or a
  restated common optional field, which keeps its canonical type. Enum values keep canon's exact spelling: non-empty
  strings without surrounding whitespace, unique within the field. Map: cmd.runtime.approve and cmd.runtime.decline
  define both the node approval shape and the HITL-038 chat-tool shape, through conditional identity exemptions that
  require blocked_sequence and allowed_action_id on every approval_kind branch except chat_tool and forbid them on
  chat_tool; canon names only the chat_tool value of approval_kind, so the definition marks that field a gap. Owner
  states maintenance_cutoffs_pending (DL-403, and since the DL-446 and DL-447 cutoffs the hold until their
  approvals pass) and dedup_hold_pending (DL-444, DL-445) map to not_configured. The thirteen CRAU-095 local-runtime
  reason codes and the UCC-111 safe-point retry states safe_point_missing and state_changed map to closed codes;
  canon names those codes without giving them closed codes, so each mapping is a worker's choice under DL-333
  resolution 6 as the stream C lead applies it, and four CRAU-095 mappings are asked of the CRAU owner
  (crau_owner_questions). A definition may tie the owner states it shows to their codes in owner_state_codes. identity_aliases lets gist_id stand for memory_item_id
  (UCC-084..UCC-088) and investigation_id for debug_session_id (UCC-077..UCC-083) without renaming canon. Canon
  already decided three further map corrections, made here with their sources: cmd.terminal.focus_session,
  compose.save_scenario, compose.run_scenario, set_context and set_namespace are recorded aliases with no
  definition; cmd.runtime.locate_and_verify_recovery and cmd.runtime.abandon_recovery are pre-attempt admissible, so
  they never require attempt_id; and worktree_lifecycle_state is required when a command mutates worktree state, as
  the overlay cell says, rather than for every domain action, so cmd.git.worktree.request_prune, which never mutates
  worktree state (GI-041), does not carry it. This entry was amended in place on 2026-11-07, before it reached main,
  after rounds 2 and 3 of the review (round_2_changes, round_3_changes), and on 2026-11-08 after the first,
  second and fifth max reviews (max_review_changes), which add to non_definition_tokens the two assistant worktree
  compatibility aliases CV-160 records, cmd.chat.worktree.create_pr and cmd.chat.worktree.open_files, the two
  worktree compatibility spellings canon targets, cmd.worktree.provision to cmd.git.worktree.create and
  cmd.worktree.release to cmd.git.worktree.release (CS-066, UCC-145), and the safe-point compatibility alias
  cmd.orchestrator.restore_safe_point_then_retry, whose exact contract names the wrapper
  cmd.orchestrator.safe_point_retry as its alias_of_command_id and normalizes it to
  cmd.runtime.restore_safe_point_then_retry (UCC-111). Jared's only words remain "approve all" (DL-333). The coordinator's
  ruling, quoted verbatim in coordinator_resolutions, is the only coordinator resolution in this entry; how it was
  applied, the lead's implementation of resolution 2, the workers' own calls, the application of DL-333 resolution 6
  and the lead's proposals are listed separately and labelled by who made them. This entry changes no owner-doc
  definition; the per-slice fixers bring the definitions to these rules.
coordinator_resolutions:
  - "Ruling (pm-mail 1107140349-9370, pm7-build, 2026-11-07T14:03Z), verbatim: \"All five as you recommend, recorded as coordinator resolutions under DL-333/DL-341. (1) (a): an identity exemption for the HITL-038 chat-tool branch, with both shapes defined; don't leave chat-tool approval without a command. (2) Yes to all three. Add checker rules so every judgment has a key, a choice and a gap_note, and no judgment can claim canon provenance; reviewers check judgments the same way as fields. (3) Yes. (4) Yes: aliases, never renaming canon. (5) Out of this branch, but not dropped: Jared wants everything finalized, so the eight unrouted ids become a follow-up packet (Q5b) in your queue, done before the final reseal.\""
resolutions_as_applied:
  - "How the P0b worker applied resolution 1 (cmd.runtime.approve and cmd.runtime.decline, round 1 S4 C1, option a): UCC-230 identity_exemptions records, for each command, blocked_sequence and allowed_action_id as conditional exemptions (condition required_when, branch_field approval_kind, exempt_branch chat_tool). The definition lists them, keeps both fields with required_when on the node branch, and offers the chat_tool branch in a required approval_kind enum, so both the OrchestratorNodeApprovalRequestV1 shape and the RuntimeApproveV3ToolRequest or RuntimeDeclineV3ToolRequest shape are defined. P0c added that both fields are forbidden on the chat_tool branch and that approval_kind is a gap field (round_2_changes)."
  - "How the P0b worker applied resolution 2 (format): the optional judgments list, nullable: true on a field, and enum values in canon's own spelling. The checker validates the judgments shape, that each key names a part of the definition (or, for omitted:, a field it does not have), a non-blank choice and gap_note, and unique keys."
  - "How the P0b worker applied resolution 3 (maintenance hold, AMS-141): owner state maintenance_cutoffs_pending maps to closed code not_configured in UCC-230 owner_state_code_map, citing DL-403, so the reason is machine-readable without widening the closed set."
  - "How the P0b worker applied resolution 4 (identity names): UCC-230 identity_aliases records gist_id for memory_item_id (UCC-084..UCC-088) and investigation_id for debug_session_id (UCC-077..UCC-083), each with canon evidence the checker finds outside UCC-230 and that names the canon name. The checker types and requires the canon name as the overlay name it stands for and refuses a definition that carries both names."
  - "Resolution 5 (ids outside UCC-049..UCC-105 that round 1 found unrouted, R1-DECISIONS call 5) is not applied in this entry; a follow-up packet Q5b settles them before the final reseal."
lead_implementation_of_resolution_2:
  - "The stream C lead's implementation of resolution 2's \"no judgment can claim canon provenance\" (P0b task text, 2026-11-07T14:04Z), not the coordinator's words: (a) no judgment may carry a provenance key, even gap; (b) a canon field whose source or gap_note contains the word JUDGMENT in any case is a C11 finding; (c) a definitions block whose fence holds a YAML comment with that word is a C11 finding."
  - "The lead's round 2 change to (c) (P0c task text, after round 2 S6 finding 7): any YAML comment in a definitions block is a C11 finding, whatever it says, because comments are invisible to tools and a word list cannot tell a choice from a note."
worker_calls:
  - "P0b worker's call, kept by the lead: for a fixed key, a judgment's choice equals the definition's own value (set equality for the two code lists), so a stale judgment cannot survive a later edit."
  - "P0b worker's reading of resolution 1, kept by the lead: a conditional exemption is mandatory, so a definition that keeps only the node shape fails; read from \"don't leave chat-tool approval without a command\"."
  - "P0b worker's call, kept by the lead: the JUDGMENT word rule also matches JUDGEMENT and the plurals; P0c extends it to snake_case compounds such as judgment_basis (round 2 S6 finding 7)."
  - "P0b worker's classification of the worktree commands, kept by the lead: create, lock, prune, recover, release, remove, reuse and unlock mutate worktree state (lock and unlock set the git lock state; unlock's precondition is worktree_locked); request_prune and select do not (select persists per-project selection and filter state, which W-075 keeps an owner runtime/view record)."
  - "P0c worker's calls: the checker enforces that approval_kind is a gap field, and a forbidden_when on the chat_tool branch may not also forbid a branch that requires the field; nullable is refused on a required row-group identity even where an identity exemption lets the definition leave the field out, since an exemption makes the field omissible, not nullable; a [] step in any judgment path must name a list field of the definition; a list choice may not repeat an entry; a whole-line YAML comment is reported against the definition of the next content line; owner_state_code_map may not map one owner state twice; the review-reference rule's list of names, read from the brief's examples and \"and the like\" (the Q5 design's sections and the fix reports' canon-conflict labels included, a future compile review not); the closed code chosen for each CRAU-095 code; and leaving CRAU-095's compatibility vocabulary unmapped (under_dl333_resolution_6)."
  - "P0d worker's calls (round 3): keeping blocked_state_required for compose_invalid, compose_service_missing, image_missing and k8s_rollout_blocked, where canon reads two ways (crau_owner_questions); the closed codes for the two UCC-111 states, safe_point_missing to blocked_state_required and state_changed to stale_projection; and not adding storage failure, source verification failure or missing explicit confirmation to the map, since canon names them only in prose and no owner-state token spells them (open_owner_questions)."
  - "Max-review fixer's calls (max_review_changes): cmd.chat.worktree.create_pr targets cmd.chat.worktree.pr, the six's Create PR command, since CV-160 names no target among the six; cmd.chat.worktree.open_files targets cmd.git.worktree.open, the catalog's side of a canon conflict: CV-160 lets it route to the canonical assistant worktree commands, none of which opens files, while UCC-058 routes Open Files through the project-scope cmd.git.worktree.open and the section 2.5C rules let the thread-scoped family normalize to project-scope worktree operations, and the catalog keeps aliases. Each alias is recorded on its target's definition."

Canon names both targets, so neither is a worker's call. Second max review finding 3."
  - "non_definition_tokens (max_review_changes, fifth max review): cmd.orchestrator.restore_safe_point_then_retry, a compatibility alias of cmd.runtime.restore_safe_point_then_retry (UI_Command_Catalog.md exact recovery command contracts table: \"`normalization.kind = compatibility_alias`, `normalizes_to_contract = cmd.runtime.restore_safe_point_then_retry`, `alias_of_command_id = cmd.orchestrator.safe_point_retry`\"; the catalog's Orchestrator safe-point retry prose: \"`cmd.orchestrator.restore_safe_point_then_retry` remains a compatibility alias for that same runtime command\"; UCC-111 canonical_text: \"The compatibility alias cmd.orchestrator.restore_safe_point_then_retry has no second handler or authority\"). Its immediate alias_of_command_id is the wrapper cmd.orchestrator.safe_point_retry, whose own contract is normalization.kind wrapper with alias_of_command_id null, so the wrapper stays a wrapper and is not listed. Canon names the runtime target, so it is not a worker's call. Fifth max review finding 2."
under_dl333_resolution_6:
  - "DL-333 resolution 6, verbatim with its scope: \"owner disabled states outside the overlay's closed set (the GitHub_Integration worktree states and the prd_planning_runtime_contracts.json codes) map to closed disabled-reason codes through UCC-230 owner_state_code_map; the owner word stays display detail and the closed set is not expanded.\" Its scope names only the GitHub_Integration worktree states and the prd_planning_runtime_contracts.json codes. Extending it to other owner states is the stream C lead's application, not the resolution's words: it rests on UCC-230's general sentence \"Owner disabled states that fall outside the closed set map to closed codes through owner_state_code_map and stay display detail\". No new ruling."
  - "Applied to the thirteen codes of the CRAU-095 canonical local-runtime reason-code base enum (the stream C lead's P0c task text, round 2 S1 finding 6 and map item 1). CRAU-095 and Containers_Registry_and_Unraid.md section 2B list the names only; every one of the thirteen mappings is the P0c worker's choice from the code's name, and each map entry says so. runtime_context_missing, k8s_context_missing, k8s_namespace_missing and access_url_unresolved map to not_configured; runtime_context_unreachable and k8s_context_unreachable to unreachable; buildx_unavailable and bake_unavailable to partial_capability; container_unhealthy to degraded: nine codes inside the shared Docker/Kubernetes disabled-state taxonomy (UCC-053; UI_Command_Catalog.md section 2.5B). compose_invalid, compose_service_missing, image_missing and k8s_rollout_blocked map to blocked_state_required, outside that taxonomy; their entries cite UCC-053 and section 2.5B beside Containers_Registry_and_Unraid.md section 2B, and the choice is asked of the CRAU owner (crau_owner_questions). Canon passages cited beside a mapping where they exist: section 2A Runtime access URL resolution (access_url_unresolved), section 2A buildx readiness (buildx_unavailable), CRAU-093 (compose_invalid, compose_service_missing), CRAU-099 (runtime_context_missing, runtime_context_unreachable) and section 2B's local-runtime blockers (runtime_context_missing, k8s_context_unreachable, container_unhealthy). CRAU-095's compatibility vocabulary is not a second base enum and is not mapped."
  - "Applied to the UCC-111 safe-point retry states (the stream C lead's P0d task text, round 3 S4 map item U1): UCC-111 and the Orchestrator safe-point retry row keep the pre-modal disabled reasons safe_point_missing, state_changed, permission_denied and operation_in_progress; the last two were already mapped (GI-041). safe_point_missing maps to blocked_state_required and state_changed to stale_projection, both the P0d worker's choice; the state_changed entry also cites the storage fallback divergence dispositions' closed disabled reasons, which include state_changed."

  - "No review or evidence reference in a definitions block (S1 finding 9, S3 finding 7): a string that names review rounds or findings, fix rounds or their reports, review files, the defs-review or owner-answers folders, the evidence share, the Q5 design's sections or the fix reports' canon-conflict labels is a C11 finding; canon text stands on canon. A unit fence's source_lineage may keep evidence paths. 49 such strings remained at 0dd32a1253."

  - "Restated common fields (S3 map item M3): a definition may restate a common optional field, required or optional, only with its canonical type and narrowing constraints. This supersedes the Q5 DESIGN.md section 4.3 rule that a restatement may only make the field required: true or add constraints; the checker already enforced the type."

crau_owner_questions:
  - "Docker/Kubernetes disabled reasons (asked of the Plans/Containers_Registry_and_Unraid.md owner): may Docker Manager command availability use blocked_state_required, outside the six-family taxonomy of UCC-053 and UI_Command_Catalog.md section 2.5B (Unsupported, Not configured, Unauthorized, Unreachable, Degraded, Partial capability), for compose_invalid, compose_service_missing, image_missing and k8s_rollout_blocked? Containers_Registry_and_Unraid.md section 2B calls compose-up failure, unhealthy container, missing Docker context, cluster unreachable and rollout failure local-runtime blockers under a blocked/degraded classification, and CRAU-103 keeps unproven states manual-only, blocked, degraded or partial capability. Until the owner answers, the map keeps blocked_state_required for those four; if the taxonomy is binding, the nearest families are not_configured for the compose and image codes and degraded for k8s_rollout_blocked."
  - "Do the other nine CRAU-095 mappings (the P0c worker's choice by name) match the owner's meaning, in particular access_url_unresolved to not_configured and buildx_unavailable and bake_unavailable to partial_capability?"
open_owner_questions:
  - "Legacy cmd.docker.remove (for the Q5b follow-up packet under resolution 5): UI_Command_Catalog.md section 2.5A still lists cmd.docker.remove as Remove Container, and that section's boundary normalizes legacy Docker rows into the canonical families with no new payload shape, while the current registration is cmd.docker.container.delete (UCC-049). Canon names no target for this row, so UCC-230 gives it no disposition and no definition records it as an alias. Q5b adjudicates it as a compatibility alias of cmd.docker.container.delete or a retirement, and records that in UCC-230 non_definition_tokens before the final reseal. Raised by the stream C lead after the fourth Sol 6.1 max review."
  - "Local or registered-host Docker target (asked of the Containers_Registry_and_Unraid.md CRAU-116 and UI_Command_Catalog.md UCC-105 owners): UCC-105 keeps the existing cmd.docker.run and cmd.docker.container.open on the HostCapabilityCommand envelope 'where exact semantics match', and CRAU-116's definitions read that as a target on a registered host: a dispatch from the Docker Manager row with neither host_capability_ref nor host_profile_id is local and builds no envelope, while one from the Docker/Hosts destination or another UCC-105 envelope caller without either ref is refused with invalid_args. Canon names no source_surface value for either case. Which values mark a local Docker Manager dispatch and which a host dispatch? Raised by the stream C lead after the third recheck of the Sol 6.1 max fixes."
  - "Host command execution context (asked of the Contracts_V0.md CV-304 and UI_Command_Catalog.md UCC-105 owners): CV-304's canonical text lists execution_unit_context among the HostCapabilityCommand fields, its acceptance criterion does not, and UCC-105 spells it execution_unit_context_ref. CRAU-116's definitions carry it only when an execution unit dispatches a host command (cmd.docker.host.session.launch from its arg; runtime attribution 'where applicable', Contracts_V0.md Runtime attribution ownership split) and none on a GUI dispatch. Which typed carrier gives an executor or orchestrator dispatch of preflight, start, stop, restart, retain or open_app, and of cmd.docker.run or cmd.docker.container.open when they target a registered host, its execution unit context, for example the UCC-230 envelope's run_id and attempt_id? Raised by the stream C lead after the second recheck of the Sol 6.1 max fixes."
  - "Assistant worktree button visibility (asked of the assistant-chat-design.md owner): ACD-322 (canonical text and acceptance criterion) and W.1's behavior rules (assistant-chat-design.md:2962) hide the Worktree button when the active project has no git repository, while CV-159 (Contracts_V0.md) keeps projectIsGitRepo only as the original Git-reader guard and never as a universal test that excludes an admitted Jujutsu route. ACD-637's six cmd.chat.worktree.* definitions follow CV-159 and cite both. Should ACD-322 and W.1 show the button for an admitted Jujutsu project? Raised by the stream C lead after the recheck of the Sol 6.1 max fixes."
  - "Known-37 recovery-unavailable rows (asked of the UI_Command_Catalog.md Known-37 and Contracts_V0 recovery-unavailable owners): the catalog says disabled projections retain \"the exact owner reason, including stale projection, permission/storage failure, operation in progress, source verification failure, or missing explicit confirmation\", but names no owner-state token for storage failure, source verification failure or missing explicit confirmation. The recovery_unavailable_resolution_receipt reason_code enum (Plans/storage_value_registry.json) has storage_read_only, storage_io_exhausted, recovery_source_not_verified and explicit_confirmation_required, which are result reasons, not disabled states. Which tokens are those disabled states? Until an owner names them, the map has no entry for them and the definitions keep their gap-note mappings."
  - "Browser control rows' owner request (asked of the Section15_MVP_Promoted_Features_Spec.md owner and the owner of Plans/section15_browser_program_contracts.schema.json): the wiring rows of cmd.browser.share_with_agent, cmd.browser.revoke_share_with_agent, cmd.browser.take_over, cmd.browser.pause_agent, cmd.browser.let_agent_continue and cmd.browser.stop_agent_keep_browser name BrowserActionRequestV2, whose command_id enum lists them, but the request requires a closed browser_action whose action_type enum holds page and tab primitives only: no share, revoke-share, takeover or agent-control action, and no field for share's thread_id or take_over's takeover_choice. Sharing and revoking change browser-session share state only and are not captures (UI_Command_Catalog.md capture event rules; Section15 browser click/highlight/share rules). The same holds for cmd.browser.detach_browser_tab, cmd.browser.open_devtools, cmd.browser.toggle_devtools_dock, cmd.browser.focus_browser_tab, cmd.browser.promote_to_normal_browsing, cmd.browser.reopen, cmd.browser.retry and cmd.browser.keep_closed, which have no detach, DevTools, dock, session-tab reveal, promotion or session-recovery action and, for open_devtools, toggle_devtools_dock, focus_browser_tab and promote_to_normal_browsing, no field for mode, dock, where, by, background or target_workspace_tab_id. SMPFS-328's definitions keep the wired request, map these fourteen commands onto no action_type, never turn share or revoke into a capture, and have a handler refuse them with handler_unavailable. Should BrowserActionRequestV2 gain session-control actions with those fields, should these commands name a different owner request, or should the two layout-only rows (toggle_devtools_dock, focus_browser_tab) be handled by the shell with no owner request? The request also has no field for the capture rows' optional thread_id, which SMPFS-328 leaves on the UICommand envelope, or for the four screenshot rows' scope (clip or full), which SMPFS-328 keeps as an arg; SMPFS-328 maps the screenshot rows to action_type screenshot and the pick-element and add-selection rows to snapshot, as its own choices. Raised in the fix round after the second Sol 6.1 max review, at the stream C lead's request."
  - "Goal Mode request editions (asked of the Goal_Runtime_System.md owner and the owners of the UI_Command_Catalog.md Simplified Goal Runtime registration rows, its section 2.7.1 Goal rows and Plans/Wiring_Matrix.production.json): GRS-086 admits a Goal in an app thread with project_id=null, and CV-366 selects the application editions for its start and update (the app.goal_start.v1 and app.goal_update.v1 graphs, input root GoalCommandRequestApplicationV1, update branch GoalCommandRequestApplicationV2), while the Project editions GoalStartRequestV2 and GoalUpdateRequestV2 stay exact. The rows name one edition each: cmd.chat.goal.update's registration and 2.7.1 rows name only GoalUpdateRequestV2 and its wiring row the scope-neutral ChatOwnerCommandRequestV2, and cmd.chat.goal.start's wiring and registration rows name only GoalStartRequestScopeV2, which resolves to the application root, while Goal_Runtime_System.md:262 and the Original Goal creation command settlement passage before GRS-066 (Goal_Runtime_System.md:6337) name GoalStartRequestV2. GRS-218's definitions keep the wired requests and select the owner input of the thread's actual scope: a Project thread's start builds GoalStartRequestV2 and its update GoalUpdateRequestV2, and an app thread's start and update build the application editions, with no Project identity and no null-to-Project rebinding. Should the registration, 2.7.1 and wiring rows name both editions of each command, and which edition marker does a UICommand dispatch carry? GRS-218 uses each edition's own schema_id for the update and the thread's scope for the start. Raised in the fix round after the fifth Sol 6.1 max review, at the closure lead's request."
